Job Summary

Management Analyst

Aptive Resources is seeking a Management Analyst to support health system transformation, implementation and operations, and healthcare business-enabling services for the Office of Suicide Prevention within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA). This role will focus heavily on supporting analysis of the efficacy of implementation of the Emergent Suicide Care benefit (ESCb) to ensure eligible Veterans receive the benefit appropriately.

This position supports VA’s implementation of the ESCb as part of the legislatively mandated COMPACT Act of 2020 requirements. This project focuses on supporting full benefit implementation through development of standard operating procedures, evaluation of benefit implementation processes across VHA offices, data analysis to support leadership decision-making, and development of communication artifacts to raise awareness of the ESCb.

This position is well suited for a consultant who thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments, and demonstrates adaptability, perseverance, and strong interpersonal skills. The candidate should also be comfortable working in a sensitive, mission-driven environment where suicide prevention and related topics are regularly discussed.

In this role, you will support program design, audits, and evaluations across a range of task areas including program analysis, data analysis, strategy development, meeting coordination, metrics development, and risk management. You will be expected to organize and prioritize work effectively, manage multiple assignments simultaneously, and remain adaptable as client needs evolve.

Primary Responsibilities

Program & Process Evaluation

  • Conduct research and structured reviews of documentation, policies, standard operating procedures, and guidance to evaluate program performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Conduct organizational assessments and gap analyses comparing current and target states, documenting findings and recommendations.
  • Apply critical, analytical, and creative thinking to help define and refine project and program requirements, objectives, and strategies.
  • Support day-to-day program execution by tracking deliverables, maintaining project artifacts and workplans, and coordinating activities across team members and stakeholders.
  • Present findings, analyses, and proposed solutions in client-facing meetings and working sessions, adapting communication style to engage internal and external audiences.
  • Coordinate and collaborate across multidisciplinary, geographically dispersed teams, establishing and maintaining constructive professional relationships with stakeholders.
  • Demonstrate initiative and perseverance by independently managing tasks, following through on assignments, and navigating obstacles to drive progress.

Data Evaluation & Analysis

  • Perform detailed qualitative analyses of program documentation, data, and stakeholder input, breaking down complex information to identify insights and develop clear, actionable, well-supported recommendations.
  • Support quantitative data review and basic metrics development to complement qualitative findings and inform program evaluation.
  • Prepare and maintain accurate documentation, records, presentations, and analytical deliverables, ensuring information is clearly communicated and appropriately formatted.
  • Continuously build and apply relevant knowledge, quickly getting up to speed on complex programmatic, policy, or operational topics to inform evaluation work.

Minimum Qualifications

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • 4+ years of relevant professional experience in management consulting, healthcare administration, project management, process engineering, business or data analysis, change management, or related fields.
  • Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, communications, management, statistics, analytics, finance, or related field.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States.

Desired Qualifications

Desired Skills and Attributes

  • Strong organizational, prioritization, analytical, and critical thinking skills, with high attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently as a self-starter, while also being an active and collaborative team participant.
  • Demonstrated capability to adapt to change, manage ambiguity, and perform effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
  • Proven ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and logically, both in writing and verbally, to a wide range of audiences.
  • Ability to synthesize qualitative information, such as interviews, document reviews, and stakeholder feedback, into clear findings, along with comfort working with quantitative data and basic metrics to support evaluation.
  • Strong commitment to professionalism, continuous learning, and relationship-building, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability for delivering high-quality work.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint) and document management best practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities for and implement improvements to processes and workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and maintain confidentiality.
  • Experience or familiarity with policy implementation in complex organizations, including translating guidance into operational processes cross-checking against applicable legislative and regulatory requirements, and supporting adoption across stakeholders.
  • Experience or familiarity with behavioral health, mental health care systems, or suicide prevention and intervention efforts, including comfort working in sensitive, mission-driven environments.
  • Prior experience supporting the VA, VHA, and/or a similar federal organization.

Physical Requirements

Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for extended periods, use a computer keyboard and mouse, and communicate verbally and in writing. The employee may occasionally need to stand, walk, bend, or lift up to 15 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.

About Aptive. Aptive partners with federal agencies to achieve their missions through improved performance, streamlined operations and enhanced service delivery. Based in Alexandria, Virginia, we support more than a dozen agencies including Veterans Affairs, Transportation, Defense, Homeland Security and the National Science Foundation. We specialize in applying technology, creativity and human-centered services to optimize mission delivery and improve experiences for millions of people who count on government services every day. jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Senior Systems Engineer (L3) at GXA is a highly experienced, hands-on escalation engineer responsible for resolving complex technical issues across a broad MSP environment. While this role brings deep expertise in networking, firewalls, and infrastructure, it is not limited to networking work. Instead, this engineer serves as the primary escalation point for the most challenging service issues and plays a critical role in strengthening overall service delivery.

This position exists to eliminate recurring escalations, reduce cross-team dependencies, and raise the technical maturity of the service organization. The Senior Systems Engineer partners closely with L1/L2 engineers, service leadership, and project teams to troubleshoot advanced issues, improve standards, and ensure stable, scalable client environments.

The ideal candidate has strong, practical networking expertise and solid mid-to-high level experience across standard MSP support, including servers, cloud services, identity, endpoint management, and core business applications. Networking escalations will be a key responsibility, but day-to-day work will span a wide range of service issues and technical mentorship.

Core Focus of the Role

  • Act as a senior escalation engineer responsible for resolving the most complex service issues across client environments, regardless of technology domain
  • Own issues through to resolution, reducing ticket reassignment, repeated escalations, and dependency on multiple teams
  • Provide deep technical support across core MSP platforms and infrastructure, including servers, cloud services, identity, endpoints, and networking
  • Serve as the primary escalation point for advanced networking and firewall issues when they arise, ensuring rapid and accurate resolution

Key Responsibilities

Advanced Technical Execution

  • Serve as the final escalation point for complex service and infrastructure issues across client environments, spanning servers, cloud services, identity, endpoints, and networking
  • Diagnose and resolve advanced issues across common MSP platforms, including:
    • Microsoft 365, Azure, and identity services
    • Active Directory, Exchange, and core server infrastructure
    • Virtualization platforms and hybrid environments
    • Networking and firewalls as a primary technical strength
  • Own troubleshooting end-to-end, from root cause analysis through resolution, without unnecessary dependency on other teams

Infrastructure & Networking Specialization

  • Act as the lead escalation engineer for advanced networking issues when required, including:
    • Firewalls (Fortinet, SonicWall, Meraki, etc.)
    • VLANs, routing, switching, VPNs, NAT, and site-to-site connectivity
  • Design, configure, and troubleshoot infrastructure that spans on-prem, cloud, and hybrid environments, ensuring stability, security, and scalability

Service Impact & Operational Efficiency

  • Resolve complex tickets directly rather than deferring or reassigning, improving customer experience and resolution time
  • Reduce recurring escalations by identifying systemic issues and driving permanent fixes
  • Produce clear documentation and resolution notes that raise the troubleshooting capability of L1/L2 engineers
  • Partner with service leadership to improve standards, workflows, and service velocity as GXA scales

Required Skills & Experience

  • Senior-level MSP support experience with the ability to independently resolve complex tickets across multiple technology domains
  • Proven experience working as an L3 or senior escalation engineer in a managed services environment
  • Strong, hands-on experience supporting core MSP platforms, including:
    • Microsoft 365 and Azure (identity, access, core services)
    • Active Directory, Exchange, and identity-related troubleshooting
    • Windows Server and common server roles
    • Virtualization platforms (VMware, Hyper-V, or equivalent)
    • Endpoint management and standard MSP tooling (RMM, PSA, backup, security tools)
  • Demonstrated ability to own tickets end-to-end, perform root cause analysis, and implement permanent fixes
  • Solid practical networking experience, including:
    • Firewall configuration and troubleshooting
    • VLANs, routing, switching, VPNs, and subnetting
  • Strong documentation and communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical issues to both technical teams and non-technical stakeholders

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Deep expertise in networking and firewalls within MSP client environments
  • Hands-on experience with firewall platforms such as Fortinet, SonicWall, Meraki, or similar
  • Experience designing or remediating complex or problematic client networks
  • Background supporting hybrid cloud environments and network-integrated cloud services
  • Experience mentoring or upskilling L1/L2 engineers through documentation, shadowing, or technical guidance
  • Familiarity with automation, scripting, or process improvement initiatives in an MSP
  • Experience working in organizations leveraging offshore or distributed service teams

Why This Role Matters at GXA

GXA is improving service efficiency rapidly and scaling intentionally. This role exists to stabilize and strengthen the technical core so growth does not create downstream service friction. The right hire will have immediate, measurable impact on ticket resolution speed and escalation volume.

jobs.excerpt: European roles, your afternoon hours.  No night shift.
jobs.description:
European roles, your afternoon hours. No night shift. If you recruit for foreign clients from the Philippines, this is the same game, paid per placement in euros. Open to recruiters based in Davao City and across the Philippines.

Read all of this before you apply. It's long on purpose. If this isn't you, that's completely fine, and it saves us both time.

Who we are

BC Recruitment places people in jobs across Europe: multilingual customer service, sales and support roles with some of the biggest international employers, in cities like Athens, Lisbon, Porto, Braga and Sofia. Many of these jobs come with relocation help, which makes them easier to sell to candidates.

We have around 60 open roles right now, in Dutch, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Turkish, the Nordic languages and more. Alongside those we have specialist roles, like compliance, legal and tech, that pay a lot more per placement.

You don't need to speak the candidates' languages. Every role needs English, and English is what we work in. What matters is that you know where to find people and how to get them excited about a job abroad.

Who we're looking for

People who are hungry, driven and excited about this opportunity, and who believe they can earn more on commission than they do now.

We don't care how many years you've been recruiting. Someone with 6 months of hunger can beat someone with 10 years of experience. We care about what you have personally delivered: how many placements, for what kind of roles, and how many a month.

You'll probably fit if:

  • You understand that every nationality is found differently. If one channel doesn't work for a market, you know where those people really are and go there.
  • You already have your own tools: LinkedIn, laptop, phone, and whatever else you use to recruit.
  • You want freedom: your own hours, your own place, your own methods, no boss.
  • You have real numbers: placements or sales you made yourself, and you know your monthly average.
  • You've done global or international recruitment, ideally for similar companies or the same kind of candidates: customer service, call centres, multilingual roles, relocation, tourism, hospitality.
  • You're a natural seller who finds people on your own, without leads or hand-holding.

This is NOT for you if

  • You need us to pay for tools before you can work. We don't cover anything at the start.
  • You want something to try "when you have time".
  • You need someone to tell you what to do every day.
  • You'll blame others when a client pauses a role or a candidate drops out. That's part of recruitment.
  • Most of the people you can reach need a visa. Most of our roles require candidates who can already work in the EU, and we don't offer visa support on most jobs.
  • You need a fixed income soon. There is no salary, retainer or paid trial at the start.

What you earn

  • Minimum €400 per placement. Most roles pay €400–750, and specialist roles up to €2,400.
  • You see the exact payout on every role before you work on it.
  • A placement counts once your candidate has started and the employer has paid us. Someone who accepts and then drops out is not a placement.
  • Payment usually comes 1–3 months after your candidate starts, depending on the employer. We pay by bank transfer or whatever works for you.
  • Money you've earned is always paid. We know many recruiters are afraid of not being paid. Think about it from our side: a recruiter who delivers is worth far more to us over time than any single placement. This whole system is built on trust, and we'd lose by breaking it.

If you deliver, we deliver back

Nothing is given up front. Everything grows with your results, for proven partners and agreed case by case:

  • Once you deliver, we cover tool costs such as monthly subscriptions.
  • Proven recruiters can get earlier payouts, arranged with you.
  • Consistent performers can earn a monthly base on top of commission.

The rules bend toward the people who prove themselves. This job gets better the more you deliver.

What you get from day one

  • Proper onboarding: we explain everything, the employers, the roles and how we work, and answer all your questions before you start, so you begin with confidence.
  • Full role details and answers to the questions candidates usually ask.
  • Direct contact with us whenever you have a question about a role or a candidate.
  • Total freedom over how, when and where you work.

What's realistic

  • The first weeks are about building your pipeline.
  • Once you're up and running, a below-average recruiter makes about 1 placement a month, a good recruiter 2–5, and our best recruiters 5–10. It gets easier over time: you build a pool of candidates to come back to, and people start recommending you.
  • We expect at least one placement a month once you're up and running.

How we choose

  1. You answer the questions below. We read every answer.
  2. If your answers are strong, we have a video call.
  3. If we're a fit, we onboard you.

Everyone starts with a 30-day trial. Show real progress in that month, with candidates submitted and in interviews, and you stay and grow. If not, we part ways with no hard feelings.

To apply, answer these questions

  1. Your numbers. How many placements have you made per month on average, and for which roles and countries? What was your best month?
  2. The task. We have a Dutch-speaking customer service role in Athens, and candidates must already be allowed to work in the EU. Where exactly would you find 5 of them within two weeks, and how? Name the real channels, groups or searches you'd use.
  3. Commission. Why do you prefer being paid per placement over a salary, or over how you've been paid before?
  4. Your setup. Which tools and channels do you use today? How many hours a week can you put in, and what else are you working on right now?

Apply here with your CV. Then email your answers to , with your name and country in the subject. Applications without answers aren't reviewed.

Optional: attach a voice note or video answering "Why should we pick you?" It's the quickest way for us to get to know you.

Be specific: numbers, names, real examples. Answers that sound AI-written, or that just say what you think we want to hear, are rejected.

NVIDIA is searching for a highly motivated and creative senior security firmware engineer to join the Data Center Systems Software team and secure the platform: the baseboard management controllers, microcontrollers, and silicon roots of trust the rest of the platform depends on. You will design and deliver the firmware that proves the integrity of NVIDIA's data center systems from the first instruction out of reset through attestation, update, and recovery in production, and set technical direction for work that spans silicon vendors, platform teams, and industry standards bodies.


What you'll be doing:

  • Derive security requirements for NVIDIA’s data center platforms from business needs and threat modeling.
  • Design and deliver root of trust firmware with features like secure and measured boot, attestation, provisioning of identities and cryptographic material, and secure debug.
  • Own features from architecture to code: make the trade-offs explicit, gain agreement across silicon, platform, security architecture, manufacturing, and partner teams, and deliver the implementation.
  • Implement industry security standards (eg.: SPDM, TCG DICE).
  • Lead design and code reviews, improve threat modeling, testing, CI, and release practices, and make AI agents a normal part of how the team builds firmware.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 7+ years of software and firmware engineering experience, or equivalent depth, including products built on a hardware root of trust.
  • Deep understanding of roof of trust security fundamentals: chains of trust, signing and key management, attestation, and anti-rollback.
  • Strong low-level programming skills and a deep understanding of SoC access controls (privilege levels, TrustZone, memory and bus protection).
  • Familiarity with server firmware and systems software, plus experience building automation using Python or a comparable language.
  • A record of leading technical work across teams without formal authority, including guiding other engineers on a shared deliverable.
  • Experience with modern AI and agents, including an AI-forward mindset and proactive adoption of new tools and techniques.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong preference for written communication that creates clarity and institutional memory for a distributed team.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and complexity; you make sound decisions quickly with incomplete information and course-correct without friction.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Contributions to open-source root of trust projects or to industry security standards.
  • Experience building systems with symmetric, asymmetric, and post-quantum cryptography.
  • Rust firmware experience, including bringing Rust into an existing C or C++ codebase.
  • Secure Manufacturing at scale. Security certifications such as FIPS 140-3.
  • Hardware cryptographic accelerators, secure key storage, trusted execution frameworks such as OP-TEE or Keystone, and OpenBMC.

jobs.excerpt: Multilingual recruiting for Europe, from home, paid in euros per placement.
jobs.description:
Multilingual recruiting for Europe, from home, paid in euros per placement. Open to recruiters based in Cairo and across Egypt.

Read all of this before you apply. It's long on purpose. If this isn't you, that's completely fine, and it saves us both time.

Who we are

BC Recruitment places people in jobs across Europe: multilingual customer service, sales and support roles with some of the biggest international employers, in cities like Athens, Lisbon, Porto, Braga and Sofia. Many of these jobs come with relocation help, which makes them easier to sell to candidates.

We have around 60 open roles right now, in Dutch, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Turkish, the Nordic languages and more. Alongside those we have specialist roles, like compliance, legal and tech, that pay a lot more per placement.

You don't need to speak the candidates' languages. Every role needs English, and English is what we work in. What matters is that you know where to find people and how to get them excited about a job abroad.

Who we're looking for

People who are hungry, driven and excited about this opportunity, and who believe they can earn more on commission than they do now.

We don't care how many years you've been recruiting. Someone with 6 months of hunger can beat someone with 10 years of experience. We care about what you have personally delivered: how many placements, for what kind of roles, and how many a month.

You'll probably fit if:

  • You've done global or international recruitment, ideally for similar companies or the same kind of candidates: customer service, call centres, multilingual roles, relocation, tourism, hospitality.
  • You're a natural seller who finds people on your own, without leads or hand-holding.
  • You understand that every nationality is found differently. If one channel doesn't work for a market, you know where those people really are and go there.
  • You already have your own tools: LinkedIn, laptop, phone, and whatever else you use to recruit.
  • You want freedom: your own hours, your own place, your own methods, no boss.
  • You have real numbers: placements or sales you made yourself, and you know your monthly average.

This is NOT for you if

  • You want something to try "when you have time".
  • You need someone to tell you what to do every day.
  • You'll blame others when a client pauses a role or a candidate drops out. That's part of recruitment.
  • Most of the people you can reach need a visa. Most of our roles require candidates who can already work in the EU, and we don't offer visa support on most jobs.
  • You need a fixed income soon. There is no salary, retainer or paid trial at the start.
  • You need us to pay for tools before you can work. We don't cover anything at the start.

What you earn

  • Minimum €400 per placement. Most roles pay €400–750, and specialist roles up to €2,400.
  • You see the exact payout on every role before you work on it.
  • A placement counts once your candidate has started and the employer has paid us. Someone who accepts and then drops out is not a placement.
  • Payment usually comes 1–3 months after your candidate starts, depending on the employer. We pay by bank transfer or whatever works for you.
  • Money you've earned is always paid. We know many recruiters are afraid of not being paid. Think about it from our side: a recruiter who delivers is worth far more to us over time than any single placement. This whole system is built on trust, and we'd lose by breaking it.

If you deliver, we deliver back

Nothing is given up front. Everything grows with your results, for proven partners and agreed case by case:

  • Once you deliver, we cover tool costs such as monthly subscriptions.
  • Proven recruiters can get earlier payouts, arranged with you.
  • Consistent performers can earn a monthly base on top of commission.

The rules bend toward the people who prove themselves. This job gets better the more you deliver.

What you get from day one

  • Proper onboarding: we explain everything, the employers, the roles and how we work, and answer all your questions before you start, so you begin with confidence.
  • Full role details and answers to the questions candidates usually ask.
  • Direct contact with us whenever you have a question about a role or a candidate.
  • Total freedom over how, when and where you work.

What's realistic

  • The first weeks are about building your pipeline.
  • Once you're up and running, a below-average recruiter makes about 1 placement a month, a good recruiter 2–5, and our best recruiters 5–10. It gets easier over time: you build a pool of candidates to come back to, and people start recommending you.
  • We expect at least one placement a month once you're up and running.

How we choose

  1. You answer the questions below. We read every answer.
  2. If your answers are strong, we have a video call.
  3. If we're a fit, we onboard you.

Everyone starts with a 30-day trial. Show real progress in that month, with candidates submitted and in interviews, and you stay and grow. If not, we part ways with no hard feelings.

To apply, answer these questions

  1. Your numbers. How many placements have you made per month on average, and for which roles and countries? What was your best month?
  2. The task. We have a Dutch-speaking customer service role in Athens, and candidates must already be allowed to work in the EU. Where exactly would you find 5 of them within two weeks, and how? Name the real channels, groups or searches you'd use.
  3. Commission. Why do you prefer being paid per placement over a salary, or over how you've been paid before?
  4. Your setup. Which tools and channels do you use today? How many hours a week can you put in, and what else are you working on right now?

Apply here with your CV. Then email your answers to , with your name and country in the subject. Applications without answers aren't reviewed.

Optional: attach a voice note or video answering "Why should we pick you?" It's the quickest way for us to get to know you.

Be specific: numbers, names, real examples. Answers that sound AI-written, or that just say what you think we want to hear, are rejected.

jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a hands-on Partnerships & BD expert to grow our banking, deposits, and investing partners, and to bring on the ones we haven't met yet. Most of the job, roughly 70 to 80 percent, is growing the partners we already have: bigger budgets, better economics, broader distribution. The rest is net new, mostly warm, with real outreach on the investing side where the relationships don't exist yet.

You'll work alongside our Head of Partnerships, who will continue to focus on our largest strategic partners. On those strategic partners, you'll run the operations. Across the rest of banking, deposits, and investing, you own it fully, operationally and strategically. That's what gives the Head of Partnerships room for the biggest bets, and it's what makes this seat yours.

This isn't a support role, and it isn't customer service. The job is to grow relationships, not just service them.

WHY THIS SEAT

  • A category to own. Banking, deposits, and investing partners outside our largest strategic accounts are yours, start to finish.
  • A partner, not a handoff. Our Head of Partnerships works closely alongside you for your first 90 days, and the goal is full independence by about day 120.
  • Room to shape it. You'll inherit real momentum, but the strategy in these categories is still being written, and you'll help write it.
  • Close to the media. You'll connect what partners need to placements across FinanceBuzz and our publisher network, which is where a good partnership becomes an extraordinary one.
  • Direct exposure to senior leadership on the deals that matter.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • Direct experience on the advertiser side of a financial comparison publisher, marketplace, or performance network, managing bank, deposit, or investing partners.
  • A record of growing accounts, not just servicing them. You can walk through a partner whose budget you grew and what moved it.
  • Sales DNA. You open doors and close. Warm relationships are most of it, but you're comfortable with cold outreach, especially to investing apps.
  • Ownership of the details. URL approvals, budget changes, CPA moves, placement and widget coordination: you run them yourself and nothing drops.
  • You figure it out without being pushed, and you pull in account management, product, media, analytics, compliance, legal, and finance to get it done.
  • Fluency in performance economics, including CPA, CPL, CPC, and revenue share, and the business acumen to use performance, revenue, and unit-economic data in a negotiation.
  • Strong communication, relationship building, and negotiation across several partners and opportunities at once.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Publisher experience, or enough of the language to hold the conversation.
  • Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, RIAs, or advisor networks.
  • Existing relationships with banks, fintech companies, investment platforms, or related financial-services companies.
  • Experience selling customer acquisition, media, lead generation, or performance-based marketing.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Existing partners

  • Budget growth, better unit economics, broader product coverage, and a bigger share of wallet with the partners you own.
  • The operations on our largest strategic banking partners, alongside the Head of Partnerships.
  • Partner operations from onboarding through campaign management, reporting, issue resolution, and optimization.
  • Proposals that connect a partner's goals to placements, audiences, and distribution across FinanceBuzz and our publisher network.
  • Accurate pipeline, forecasts, partner updates, and next steps.
  • Launch Potato's presence at industry events and partner meetings.

New partners

  • A pipeline across banking, deposits, investing, and wealth.
  • Reaching the right decision makers through relationships, referrals, events, and outbound.
  • Partner conversations from first outreach through pitch, deal negotiation, contracting, and launch.
  • A clear read on each partner's growth goals, economics, products, and target customers.

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE

  • First 90 days: you're learning the book side by side with the Head of Partnerships and running operations on the partners you'll own.
  • By about day 120: you run your partners independently.
  • By month 6: you're directing internal traffic and connecting partner activity to media opportunity.
  • Year one: larger budgets and stronger economics across existing partners, new banks and investing advertisers live, and the Head of Partnerships focused on our largest, most strategic deals.

THIS ISN'T THE RIGHT SEAT IF YOU

  • Want to hunt, close, and hand the account to someone else.
  • Want someone else to own the operations.
  • Need a playbook handed to you before you move.
  • Would rather service an account than grow it.

TOTAL COMPENSATION

jobs.title: Accounts Receivable Specialist
jobs.excerpt: The World We EnvisionI believe the work that gets care paid for matters as much as the work that gets a device to a patient's door.
jobs.description:
The World We Envision

I believe the work that gets care paid for matters as much as the work that gets a device to a patient's door. When cash moves fast and clean, we say yes to the next patient sooner. I want every card run the day it's ready, every work comp invoice paid, and a weekly scoreboard that shows exactly who made it happen. If you've hit your numbers somewhere that only noticed when you missed them, you'll find that's not how it works here.

The Mission and Team

Right Coast Medical started in 2010 with one question from our founder, Brent Long: "What if pain relief didn't have to come with a risk of addiction?" Back then, opioids were the default after surgery. Brent thought families deserved better, and he built a company around non-opioid recovery devices like ThermX, T-REX and SAM 2.0.

Zach Holmes joined in 2014, fresh out of college. He helped grow RCM from a regional operation into a national provider, and today he runs it as our CEO. That's what this place does for people who take ownership.

You'll work with me, our CFO, and a small billing team that takes care of veterans and injured workers across the country. They get the claims right. You make sure the money comes in.

The Role: Accounts Receivable Specialist

You turn every VA card and work comp invoice into cash, fast and right, so we can keep our promise to providers and patients, and veterans and injured workers can recover without opioids and get back to what they love.

This is a new seat. Today our billers carry the back end of billing on top of the front end, and both jobs deserve a full-time owner. Getting paid isn't a project that ends. We built this role because we need it.

You'll love:

  • Running 500–750 VA card payments a month, each one charged, receipted and posted within one business day at 98%+ accuracy
  • Raising our work comp collection rate by 15 points in your first year
  • Cutting the time it takes a work comp invoice to turn into cash by 30% in your first six months
  • Bringing old balances back to life, so every aged invoice has a status, a contact and a next step
  • Freeing our billers to focus on getting claims right the first time
  • Seeing exactly where you stand on a weekly scoreboard, with no guessing about whether you're winning

Where this leads

As RCM grows, this seat can grow into a lead role, or
move up into billing. I won't promise you a title. I will promise that your results will be seen, and that the people who get promoted here are the ones who own their numbers.

Along the way, you'll learn work comp billing end to end, from the invoice to the adjuster to the cash. You'll become the person who knows where every dollar stands and what it will take to bring it in.

About You

  • You have 2+ years of work comp, medical, or third-party collections experience. Adjusters and TPAs don't rattle you.
  • Before anything goes out, you check every amount, card and receipt.
  • Today's queue gets cleared today.
  • You follow up until it's paid: politely, on schedule, every time.
  • No open item on your desk lacks a next step and a date.
  • When an adjuster pushes back, you hold the line without caving or getting heated.
  • Patient and card data stay protected because that's your habit, not because someone is watching.
  • Excel and QuickBooks Online feel familiar. Salesforce, Breadwinner and PayTrace
    you'll learn with us.

This is not for you if:

  • You need someone checking in to stay on task. This is remote, and the scoreboard does the talking.
  • "Close enough" is close enough.
  • You'd rather send one email and wait than pick up the phone.

Pay and Terms

  • $25.00/hour to start, hourly and overtime-eligible
  • $26.44/hour at day 90, once you hit your first 90-day goals
  • Quarterly bonus of up to $1,500 ($6,000/year), tied to work comp collection results
  • Full-time, remote (U.S.), Monday–Friday, roughly 8–5 in your time zone, with some flexibility as long as you're working mostly during business hours
  • 15 days paid PTO, 5 sick days, and paid holidays
  • 401(k)

If you're reading this and saying "HECK YEAH," we want to meet you.

Salary: $25/hr

Tiro is growing with purpose.

You'll join a business with ambitious plans, a collaborative leadership team and the freedom to make meaningful change.

jobs.title: Fullstack React Native Developer
jobs.excerpt: The RoleTuneCore Engineering builds the web and mobile applications that power the world’s leading music distribution platform for independent artists.
jobs.description:
The Role

TuneCore Engineering builds the web and mobile applications that power the world’s leading music distribution platform for independent artists. We’re looking for a Fullstack React Native Developer to help build our next-generation mobile experience — someone equally comfortable shipping polished React Native features and building the Rails APIs that power them.

This is a senior-level role: you’ll own significant technical scope, set direction on mobile architecture and practices, and mentor other engineers, while staying hands-on in the codebase.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain cross-platform mobile applications using React Native for iOS and Android from a single codebase

  • Build and maintain the Rails API endpoints that power the mobile app — request/response contracts, background jobs, and data models the client depends on

  • Work closely with product, design, and backend engineers to translate designs and wireframes into high-quality, reusable code across the full stack

  • Integrate RESTful APIs and third-party SDKs; optimize app performance, responsiveness, and stability

  • Write unit and integration tests, and help shape our mobile testing strategy as we build out React Native end-to-end coverage

  • Debug and resolve platform-specific issues, including native modules and bridging

  • Manage app store submissions and release processes for both the App Store and Google Play

  • Stay current with the React Native ecosystem and mobile best practices, and bring relevant updates back to the team

  • Uphold TuneCore’s core mission, vision, and values in the code you ship and the decisions you make

Leadership Expectations

  • Provide technical leadership on mobile architecture decisions, balancing durability and scalability against delivery speed

  • Set and evolve coding standards and best practices for the mobile codebase

  • Give effective, constructive code review feedback to other engineers

  • Mentor and guide engineers on the team in both technical growth and career development

  • Research and recommend new tools and technologies where they’d meaningfully improve the team’s output

  • Skills and Attributes

  • 6+ years of experience writing production code, including 3+ years building and shipping mobile applications

  • Strong proficiency in React / React Native, and in JavaScript/TypeScript

  • Demonstrated fluency with Ruby on Rails in production — building and maintaining API-only Rails services, not just “a web framework of some kind”

  • Familiarity with state management approaches (we currently use React Query and Context API)

  • Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and mobile release workflows

  • Understanding of mobile UI/UX principles and platform guidelines (Apple HIG, Material Design)

  • Experience with REST APIs and async data handling; GraphQL a plus

  • Experience with native iOS (Swift/Objective-C) or Android (Kotlin/Java) a plus, but not required

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Salary Transparency

TuneCore is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base salary range for this position is $120,000-$135,000. The final salary offer will be determined by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s relevant experience, specialized skills, internal equity, and specific work location. This range represents our good faith estimate at the time of posting.

Where you'll be

This role will be remote. TuneCore operates on a hybrid model giving our teams flexibility and choice in how they work. Employees have the option to work from our office 8 days per month on a flexible schedule organized at the department level.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Our Values:

TuneCore is a team of creators, for creators. Our mission is to support our artists and labels at every stage of their careers. Our driving forces are fairness, expertise, respect and transparency. As global citizens, we believe that if we build more diverse, equitable and inclusive teams across our company, we will collectively create and offer more innovative solutions and better serve our artists, labels, partners, and employees.

We strive to build a company that reflects the communities we serve and embraces the diversity of the world we live in, where each person’s unique perspective is valued, and where everyone has the same opportunities and is supported in their personal and professional growth. From our hiring practices to the culture we create and nurture, we are committed to listening, learning and evolving. Our goal is to make TuneCore an inspirational place that feels comfortable and familiar no matter how you look, where you call home, who you love, what you believe, or what’s on your playlist.

CSR Strategy: Shaping Music for Good

Our core values are put into action through Shaping Music for Good, Believe and TuneCore’s global corporate social responsibility strategy, integrated at all levels of the company and at the heart of our business model.

We strive to shape the music industry for good by building trusting relationships with artists and partners, investing in the growth and talent development of our local markets, and empowering our community to positively impact society. We work to achieve progress on our core priorities: gender equity, diversity, equity & inclusion, environmental sustainability, and wellness for our employees, artists, and industry partners.

Shapers Program

Employees have the opportunity to join the Shapers Program, a resource group made up of teammates who want to dedicate their time and skills to Shaping Music For Good initiatives. Shapers develop action plans, educate teammates, support the implementation of programs, and inspire action within the organization on causes and issues that align with TuneCore and Believe’s SMFG priorities.

Inclusion in the Music Business Report

In 2025, Believe and TuneCore partnered with the Annenberg Inclusion Initiative, the world’s leading think tank studying diversity and inclusion in the entertainment industry, to produce the second Inclusion in the Music Business report which analyzes the gender, race, and ethnicity among executive leadership in the music industry.

Recognition and Awards:

  • Fast Company's 10 Most Innovative Companies in Music list (2023-2025)

  • Crain's Best Places to Work in NYC (2022-2024)

Benefits & Perks:

At TuneCore we’re committed to the well-being of our employees and aim to create a workplace that fosters both personal and professional growth. Our inclusive benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Paid Time Off including vacation, holidays, paid bereavement, unlimited paid sick days, and company-wide week off between Christmas and New Years—every employee needs time to take care of themselves and their family.

  • “Wellness Fridays” year-round (close at 1pm on Fridays)

  • Universal Paid Parental Leave for both parents - because we know your newest family member(s) deserve your undivided attention.

  • Comprehensive health, vision, dental, FSA and dependent care from day 1 of employment - your health comes first.

  • 401k match - an investment in your future.

  • Company wide events, outings and volunteer days – we have team spirit and know how to have fun!

  • Hybrid Work - employees have the option to work primarily remotely and work from the office 8 days per month on a flexible schedule organized at the department level, in accordance with Company policies.

  • Learning and development opportunities and career development training – we believe in promoting and growing our leadership from within the company and proactively invest in our people.

  • Free distribution subscription for employees – so you can experience the magic of releasing music worldwide (and give us valuable feedback!).

TuneCore and Believe are Equal Opportunity Employers. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive work environment. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Before TuneCore, artists needed to be signed to a record label to sell their music online. In 2006, we democratized the industry by partnering directly with digital stores and streaming platforms to enable any musician to sell their songs worldwide while retaining 100% ownership of their music. Today, TuneCore is the leading independent development partner for self-releasing artists to build audiences and careers, with technology and services across distribution, publishing administration and a range of promotional services. TuneCore is headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, and owned by Paris-based Believe, one of the world’s leading digital music companies. The company is one of the fastest growing companies in the music industry and is actively investing in the continued growth of the business.

We have made it our mission to best serve artists and labels at each stage of their development in the digital world. We are a company that cares deeply about our people and our creator community, advocating for diversity, equity, and inclusion across all of our platforms and throughout our business. The pursuit of innovation inspires us to work hard for our artists, while collaboration drives the way we work and approach our company’s social responsibility.

Join TuneCore as we embark on the next phase of innovation in the music industry. Be part of the team that bridges the unmet and evolving needs of creators by building the tools and services that make their lives better.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Senior Analytics Engineer builds reliable data solutions that improve decision-making, operational efficiency, and business performance across Empower. Operating in a hyper-growth, highly regulated 503A/503B environment, this individual contributor owns analytics delivery from problem definition through deployment and monitoring. The role translates ambiguous business needs into scalable, maintainable, cost-effective data models, pipelines, and reporting solutions while strengthening data quality and infrastructure reliability. Success requires strategic thinking, disciplined execution, sound technical judgment, and learning agility to balance immediate priorities with sustainable engineering practices. The engineer identifies valuable analytics opportunities, communicates findings clearly, and partners with stakeholders to align solutions with business objectives. Through mentoring, knowledge sharing, and reusable tools, this role increases team productivity and supports Empower’s mission of expanding access to high-quality medications with dependable, actionable insights that guide decisions.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Analytics Delivery and Business Impact

• Project Delivery: Lead analytics projects from problem definition through deployment and monitoring, delivering solutions aligned with business objectives and stakeholder needs.
• Opportunity Assessment: Propose analytics initiatives with data-driven business cases that clarify expected value, operational benefits, and priorities for stakeholder evaluation.
• Solution Design: Design scalable, maintainable, cost-effective data models, pipelines, and reporting solutions that resolve ambiguous business problems through structured technical analysis.

Data Quality and Operational Reliability

• Data Quality: Identify and resolve data issues, validate analytical outputs, and monitor deployed solutions to maintain reliable insights for business users.
• Infrastructure Improvement: Improve data infrastructure and engineering workflows to reduce recurring issues, increase processing efficiency, and sustain reliable analytics delivery.
• Engineering Discipline: Maintain version-controlled code and solution documentation to support consistent maintenance, accountable changes, and reliable analytics in regulated operations.

Technical Leadership and Collaboration

• Technical Mentorship: Mentor junior team members through technical guidance and knowledge sharing, strengthening problem-solving capability and consistent analytics engineering practices.
• Reusable Solutions: Develop shared tools and libraries that reduce duplicated effort, improve engineering consistency, and increase team productivity across analytics projects.
• Stakeholder Alignment: Partner with business stakeholders to clarify requirements, communicate insights through effective data storytelling, and adapt solutions to evolving priorities.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:

• Proficiency in Python, SQL, and data modeling methods, including Kimball and Data Vault 2.1, for scalable, maintainable analytics solutions.
• Technical proficiency with Apache Hop, dbt, Snowflake, AWS, and Azure to build reliable data pipelines and improve infrastructure efficiency.
• Ability to use Power BI, DAX, and data storytelling to communicate actionable insights and explain technical findings to varied stakeholders.
• Skill in Git, conceptual modeling with LucidChart, structured problem-solving, and technical mentoring to support maintainable solutions, knowledge sharing, and team productivity.

EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

• At least 5 years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or a related role delivering practical business solutions required.
• A bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience required.
• Knowledge of the pharmacy business and Certified Data Vault 2.0 Practitioner certification for translating business requirements into structured data models required.
• Certified DBT Developer and Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst (PL-300) certifications, demonstrating analytics development and reporting expertise highly preferred.
• Snowflake experience or SnowPro certification, along with AWS Data Engineering or AWS Data Analytics certification supporting cloud analytics delivery preferred.

Job Description:

The Principal Analytics Engineer provides advanced analytics and data engineering support across multiple business and program areas. This role sits at the intersection of data engineering, analytics, and business intelligence—designing scalable data pipelines and analytics-ready datasets while delivering dashboards and analytical models that drive data-informed decisions and operational efficiency.

This position is fully remote and requires a Public Trust (or the ability to obtain it). US citizenship required. The candidate may be required to work outside of business hours, including weekends, based on need.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain automated, scalable ETL/ELT data pipelines using Python, SQL, and cloud-based tools to integrate, transform, and validate structured and unstructured data from diverse sources.
  • Develop and manage analytics-ready data models and workflows (e.g., in Databricks or similar platforms) to support reporting, self-service analytics, and advanced data science use cases.
  • Implement CI/CD practices using GitLab for data workflows, ensuring reliable, versioned, and repeatable analytics and data engineering processes.
  • Design, develop, and deploy interactive dashboards and reports using Tableau, Power BI, or similar tools to deliver complex analysis and actionable insights to business and technical stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

The Engagement Services Consultant (ESC), Integrations is a new, consultant-level role within Samsara's Engagement Services team in Customer Success. You will partner directly with our largest Enterprise customers in a focused, roughly three-month engagement to understand their operational processes, map how those processes connect to the Samsara platform, and translate that understanding into a well-defined, build-ready request for our Solutions Integration Services (SIS) team.

This role complements the Engagement Services Manager (ESM) and SIS teams. It ensures every integration request reaches SIS with validated requirements, aligned stakeholders, and documented processes. This role can be office-based or fully remote.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Mexico

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

. Discover and define processes (weeks 1–6)

  • Run structured discovery with customer stakeholders to document current-state processes and systems.
  • Facilitate workshops to map future-state process flows and identify where data must be sent, received, or transformed.
  • Build a systems and API inventory covering data volumes, authentication constraints, and regulatory or data-residency considerations.
  • Engage SIS early for lightweight feasibility checks so blockers surface before build.
  1. Package requirements (weeks 6–10)
  • Turn findings into a prioritized requirements package: use cases, field-level data mappings, success criteria, and open risks.
  • Validate the package with customer stakeholders and the internal account team (CSM, ESM, Sales Engineer).
  • Complete and submit the SIS Request Log so scoping starts from a validated baseline.
  1. Hand off and transition (weeks 10–12)
  • Join the initial SIS/ESM scoping meeting to preserve context and answer requirements questions directly.
  • Support the ESM during SOW drafting where scope or customer intent needs clarification.
  • Formally close the discovery engagement once SIS and the ESM confirm the request is ready for build, with documentation handed off in full.

Ongoing

  • Track engagement status, milestones, and timelines in Salesforce and Compass.
  • Maintain a library of discovery templates and playbooks by integration type, and share lessons learned with the teams that originate requests.
  • Champion Samsara's cultural principles: Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Speed - Short time from kickoff to a request SIS accepts without further scoping clarification
  • Quality - Requests that need no rework during SIS and ESM scoping.
  • Cycle time - Faster path from Request Log to signed SOW compared with baseline.
  • Customer experience - Strong discovery-phase CSAT and feedback from Enterprise stakeholders.
  • Portfolio impact - More Enterprise accounts moving from an unscoped integration need to a signed, in-build SIS project each quarter.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 7+ years in a customer-facing consulting, business/systems analysis, solutions consulting, or implementation role, ideally in enterprise SaaS or IoT software.
  • Experience running structured discovery with enterprise customers: stakeholder interviews, current- vs. future-state process mapping, and requirements gathering.
  • Working understanding of APIs and system-integration concepts; comfortable in technical conversations without needing to write integration code.
  • Strong facilitation, synthesis, and documentation skills, with the ability to turn cross-functional conversations into an actionable requirements document.
  • Track record managing multi-month, multi-stakeholder engagements independently, with ownership of timeline and quality.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience with integrations involving fleet/telematics, ERP, WMS, TMS/dispatch, HRIS, or fuel-card systems.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce and services/project-tracking tools.
  • Background as a Solutions Consultant, Sales/Solutions Engineer, Professional Services consultant, or Business/Systems Analyst.
  • Experience supporting Mexico and broader LatAm Enterprise accounts.

YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

  • Shadow the ESM and SIS teams on 2–3 active integration engagements to learn the Request Log, scoping, and SOW process end to end.
  • Complete SIS Office Hours and Request Log training, and review prior SIS project documentation for common integration patterns.
  • Take ownership of a first discovery engagement with an Enterprise account, with an ESM as coach.
  • Deliver a first fully validated requirements package and SIS Request Log independently by the end of the quarter.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

As Proof expands from the online notarization category we created into portable digital identity and agentic authorization, our brand needs to grow with us.

As Director of Brand and Creative, you'll own Proof's brand strategy, visual and verbal identity, and creative output across every touchpoint, including proof.com, campaigns, events, sales materials, and executive presence. jobs.description:
Description

The Risk Manager (Clinical Research) plays a pivotal role in developing and executing risk-based monitoring strategies, ensuring data quality and integrity in clinical research projects. This position involves cross-functional collaboration to identify, assess, and mitigate risks throughout the clinical trial lifecycle, supporting the seamless implementation of Risk-Based Study Management (RBSM) principles in a CRO or pharma industry.

RESPONSIBILITIES

More specifically, the Risk Manager must:

  • Provide subject matter expertise for developing and updating the risk-based monitoring strategy tailored to project needs.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify and mitigate risks associated with complex indications.
  • May have to coordinate with central monitor team and verify work.
  • Point sur provide budget recommendations, change orders.
  • Draft initial risk assessments and support the finalization of Risk Assessment and Categorization Tools (RACT).
  • Guide Project Managers (PMs) in transferring identified risks to the appropriate tracking systems and ensure ongoing reviews.
  • Advise on developing functional plans to mitigate risks effectively.
  • Utilize available tools to conduct remote data reviews and centralized statistical monitoring, identifying risks to data quality and integrity.
  • Facilitate internal and sponsor reviews of findings, seeking cross-functional support for complex risks and mitigations.
  • Deliver initial and ongoing training for study teams on risk assessment, centralized monitoring, and risk-based monitoring strategies.
  • Escalate risks or deliverables at risk to the PM, including scope changes.
  • Provide strategic input on risk characterization and reporting to leadership.
  • Take on additional responsibilities as required, ensuring qualifications and training align with assigned tasks.

Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Requirements

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to clinical research;

Experience

  • Must have experience in a CRO or pharma industry
  • Minimum of 3 years in risk management within a clinical research setting.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience across clinical monitoring, data management, drug safety.

Requirements:

  • Expertise in Good Clinical Practice/ICH E6 (R3) Guidelines and other regulatory requirements.
  • Proficiency in Risk-Based Monitoring strategies, processes, and tools.
  • Mastery of MS Excel (sorting, filtering, pivot tables).
  • Advanced skills in analytical data visualization tools.
  • Knowledge of Lean Six Sigma and web based RACT tools.
  • Strong analytical and statistical understanding.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and leadership skills.
  • Ability to anticipate critical issues and develop proactive contingency plans.
  • Skilled in project workflows and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Training, mentoring, and organizational capabilities.
  • High level of autonomy.
  • Fluent in English (excellent oral and written).
  • Must be able to communicate clearly and effectively at all levels within the organization and with external customers.
  • Must be a fast learner and able to understand new concepts quickly.
  • Prioritization skills with the ability to plan, monitor, and manage workload fluidly in response to changing project demands.
  • Excellent understanding of project protocol, project documentation including centralized monitoring and risk-based monitoring.
  • Broad working knowledge of the roles, functions and process of conducting clinical trials.
  • Must be able to manage time effectively, working with multiple functions and requirements.
  • Must have been involved in the use of trial management or data management systems.

Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company

OUR COMPANY

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Flexible work schedule
  • Permanent full-time position
  • Ongoing learning and development

About Indero

Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale..

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

Indero only accepts applicants who can legally work in Czech Republic.

jobs.description:
⌘ Role Overview

The Enablement & Operations Manager owns the systems, processes, and enablement that allow Customer Support and Trust & Safety to run consistently and at scale. The role spans two connected areas: Enablement (knowledge and documentation standards, onboarding and training, and ownership of the quality programme) and Operations (tooling, Zendesk configuration, automation and AI-assisted workflows, taxonomies, and reporting).

This is a hands-on leadership role. You are the point of accountability for how the CX function operates day to day, expected to independently identify gaps, propose solutions, and drive them through to implementation. You stay close to reality through system monitoring, dashboards, and quality insight rather than frontline ticket handling, and you line-manage a QA Analyst.

⌘ Key Responsibilities

Enablement, Knowledge & Training

  • Own the Help Centre and internal support documentation standards, including macros, workflows, and SOPs.
  • Own onboarding and ramp frameworks and set training priorities so representatives are consistently well-equipped.
  • Keep knowledge content accurate, current, and easy for the team to apply, closing gaps proactively.

Quality

  • Own the QA framework and standards across the CX function.
  • Line-manage a QA Analyst, and turn quality findings into coaching, content, process, and automation improvements.

CX Systems, Tooling & Automation

  • Own CX tooling standards and Zendesk system configuration: routing, triggers, automations, and escalation logic across Customer Support and Trust & Safety.
  • Lead the continuous rollout and governance of AI-assisted support and moderation workflows, including prompt configuration, automation rules, quality checks, and safeguards.
  • Own intent, sentiment, and feedback taxonomies, ensuring tagging reflects customer context and risk.
  • Monitor automation performance and decide when adjustments, safeguards, or rollbacks are needed.

Insights, Reporting & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Own CX operational dashboards and reporting standards, giving leadership timely visibility into volume, automation performance, sentiment, and trends.
  • Represent CX systems and enablement in cross-functional work with Product, Tech, Data, and Operations, supporting launches, policy, and process changes.

⌘ Expected Outcomes

Within 6–12 months, success looks like:

  • CX teams operate on clear, stable, well-governed systems and documentation.
  • Zendesk workflows, automations, and escalation paths support Customer Support and Trust & Safety without friction.
  • AI-assisted workflows are trusted, monitored, and governed, with clear quality controls.
  • The Help Centre and internal documentation are rebuilt to standard and consistently used.
  • Quality is measured through a clear framework, with the QA Analyst delivering reliable insight.
  • CX leadership has early visibility into pain points, safety risks, and operational bottlenecks.

⌘ Skills & Competencies

  • Strong understanding of CX operations and customer-facing workflows.
  • Proven experience owning CX tooling and operational systems, especially Zendesk.
  • Ability to design, test, and QA automation and AI-assisted workflows.
  • Systems-oriented thinker with strong execution discipline and attention to detail in quality- and risk-sensitive environments.
  • Data-literate, comfortable working with dashboards and operational metrics.
  • Clear communicator and effective people manager, able to influence peers and stakeholders.

⌘ Required Experience

  • 3–5+ years in CX Operations, Support Operations, or Enablement, or a closely related role.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Zendesk (configuration, workflows, routing, reporting).
  • Experience leading automation or tooling initiatives in an operational environment.
  • Experience managing or coaching others.
  • Exposure to AI-assisted support or moderation tools is a plus.
  • Strong fluency in English required.

⌘ Recruitment process

  • Introduction Interview (30min): A conversation with Talent Acquisition to discuss your experience, goals, and fit with Timeleft's mission.
  • Panel Interview (45min): A joint conversation with the Customer Support Manager and Trust & Safety Manager, the peers you'll partner with most closely.
  • Take-Home Test: A practical exercise reflecting typical operational and tooling scenarios in the role.
  • Final Interview (45min): A follow-up with the Head of Customer Experience to review your take-home and confirm alignment.

  • Establish deployment strategies, environment promotion standards, and release governance practices that support secure and reliable delivery across enterprise data platforms.
  • Contribute to technical discussions, peer reviews, and knowledge-sharing initiatives across the data engineering team.
  • Leverage AI-powered development and productivity tools to accelerate solution delivery, improve code quality, and enhance engineering productivity

Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree and 6 years of experience in Data Engineering, Data Warehousing, Cloud Data Platforms, or related technology disciplines.

OR

High School Diploma or GED and 10 years of experience in the same areas.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Advanced experience with modern data warehousing and large-scale data processing technologies such as Snowflake, Spark, or equivalent platforms.
  • Advanced proficiency in Python and SQL.
  • Advanced experience designing, developing, orchestrating, and supporting ETL/ELT pipelines and data integration solutions using tools such as dbt, Apache Airflow, Astronomer, or equivalent cloud-native data engineering technologies.
  • Advanced experience with data modeling, data warehousing, and data engineering best practices.
  • Experience designing, developing, and supporting scalable, reliable, and high-performing data engineering solutions in enterprise environments.
  • Experience collaborating with business and technology stakeholders to deliver data-driven solutions.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Following qualifications are a plus

  • Advanced experience with enterprise ETL/ELT tools such as DataStage, SAP BODS, SSIS, Informatica, or equivalent technologies.
