jobs.description:
Overview As one of the nation's leading electric transmission line construction companies, MasTec Power Delivery companies engineer and construct efficient and reliable electrical transmission, distribution, and substation & switchyard systems. Our extensive workforce includes both union and nonunion teams, which, combined with our specialized equipment fleet, allows us to effectively meet our clients' needs for power delivery, emergency restoration, and ongoing maintenance. We've been involved in some of the most challenging and recognizable electric projects across the U.S. From the electric plant to the end users, MasTec's experienced managers and crews consistently deliver transmission, distribution, and substation & switchyard services with an unfailing commitment to safety, integrity, and sustainable practices. The Geotechnical Engineer is responsible for providing geotechnical engineering support for high-voltage electric transmission and power delivery projects. This position applies geotechnical principles to the evaluation, design, and construction of foundations and other project components, helping ensure safe, reliable, constructible, and cost-effective solutions. The ideal candidate will have experience supporting infrastructure, utility, or transmission projects and will work closely with civil, structural, transmission, construction, and project management teams. The role requires sound engineering judgment, strong technical skills, and the ability to manage geotechnical assignments from investigation and analysis through design, documentation, and construction support. salary range: $120-150k depending on experience Responsibilities Perform geotechnical investigations, field evaluations, and site assessments for transmission and power delivery projects. Develop and review geotechnical reports, engineering calculations, recommendations, and design documentation. Evaluate subsurface conditions and provide recommendations for transmission structure foundations and other civil infrastructure. Support foundation design, including evaluation of bearing capacity, settlement, lateral capacity, uplift, and other applicable geotechnical considerations. Coordinate with civil, structural, transmission, and construction teams to develop practical and constructible foundation solutions. Review soil and laboratory testing data and interpret geotechnical information for design applications. Provide geotechnical input for project development, cost estimates, schedules, and design decisions. Support constructability reviews and provide recommendations to address field and construction challenges. Review contractor submittals, respond to technical questions, and provide engineering support during construction as needed. Ensure geotechnical designs and recommendations comply with applicable codes, standards, project specifications, and regulatory requirements. Communicate technical findings and recommendations effectively to project teams, customers, contractors, and other stakeholders. Travel periodically to project sites, customer meetings, and field investigations as required. Perform other duties in support of project and department objectives. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline from an accredited university. Minimum 5 years of geotechnical engineering experience, preferably supporting utility, transmission, power delivery, or other heavy civil infrastructure projects. Professional Engineer (PE) license or ability to obtain one preferred. Experience with transmission structure foundation design is highly desirable. Skills & Qualifications Strong understanding of geotechnical engineering principles and foundation design. Experience evaluating subsurface conditions, soil properties, bearing capacity, settlement, uplift, and lateral loads. Familiarity with geotechnical investigation methods, soil and laboratory testing, and interpretation of field data. Knowledge of applicable geotechnical and structural design codes and standards, including IBC, ASCE, ACI, and relevant industry standards. Experience with geotechnical analysis and design software preferred. Ability to prepare and review technical reports, calculations, drawings, and specifications. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple assignments and work effectively within multidisciplinary project teams. Willingness to travel to project sites and field locations as required.

It means being immersed in a supportive culture that recognizes you as a key player in Armstrong's future. We are a large company with a local feel, where you will get to know and collaborate with leadership and your colleagues across the company.

Reporting to the Senior Marketing Strategy Manager, the Events Manager leads the development, execution, and performance tracking of the company’s event portfolio, including trade shows, conferences, and experiential events. Working in close partnership with the Senior Marketing Strategy Manager, the role defines event strategy, establishes priorities, and translates broader marketing objectives into distinctive brand experiences that engage target audiences, strengthen customer relationships, and deliver measurable marketing and business outcomes.

Combining strategic thinking, creative judgment, and operational discipline, the Events Manager directs the people, partners, and investments required for successful delivery. This leader manages the Events Supervisor and Events Specialist, partners closely with cross-functional teams, and maintains accountability for the quality, consistency, and effectiveness of the overall events portfolio.

What’s in it for you!

  • Work alongside experienced marketing professionals in a highly collaborative environment.
  • Develop and mentor a growing events team.
  • Expand your leadership, marketing, and experiential branding expertise.
  • Make a measurable impact on brand awareness, customer relationships, and business growth.

  • Foster a collaborative environment that encourages creativity, accountability, sound judgment, and continuous learning

Travel: Approximately 40%, varying based on the event calendar and business needs.

What will make you successful

We’re looking for a Licensing Coordinator to support our Licensing team.   • Prior experience with music publishing rights.
  • Prior experience in copyright research and/or administration.
  • Impeccable attention to detail.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Organized multitasker.

jobs.description:
Marketing Strategist

Client Strategy | Campaigns | Content

Location: NYC or Tri-State strongly preferred, east coast hours required (remote role)
Salary: $85,000–$95,000

Type: Full-Time

Hi, we’re Big Human. We’re a full-service digital product agency. We work with the world’s most interesting brands to bring their vision to life through technology, design, branding and marketing.

Since 2010, we’ve produced 262 websites, 80 applications and 50 brands for clients like Rockefeller Center, Gemini, Quinn and Netflix. And we’ve still found time for our own passion projects on the side (like HQ Trivia and Vine).

We’re hiring a Marketing Strategist to own client marketing programs from start to finish. You’ll work across a varied mix of clients, from cultural institutions and nonprofits to consumer platforms and enterprise B2B, plus Big Human’s own brand.

This role is for someone several years into their agency career who wants more ownership and is ready to grow fast. You’ll work closely with our Director of Marketing, who will invest in your development. In return, we’re looking for someone who takes real ownership.

About the Role

At Big Human, we’re a strategic growth partner to our clients. Our goal isn’t to do more marketing. It’s to do the right marketing.

You’ll start every project by defining what success looks like, then set clear goals and milestones to get there. You’ll estimate how long the work will take, prioritize against it, and keep clients and teammates clear on what’s happening and why.

You’ll work across channels: social, email, content and web. The right mix depends on the client and the goal, and you’ll help decide it.

AI is part of how we work. You’ll use it to explore ideas, draft and analyze. Claude often takes the first pass on a draft. Your job is to bring the taste and judgment that make it good, and to own the final result.

What You’ll Do

Client Strategy & Planning

  • Translate client goals into marketing plans with clear goals, milestones and success metrics
  • Take the first strategic pass when a project starts from scratch
  • Shape go-to-market and launch plans for new products, features and campaigns
  • Pull client inputs, research and data together into a clear direction
  • Estimate the hours work will take, then prioritize against that
  • Break plans into weekly actions so work doesn’t stall or drift
  • Make trade-offs, say “no” or “not now” when work won’t move the needle, and explain why
  • Know where each client engagement stands so the work stays focused on what matters at that stage

Campaigns & Channels

  • Plan and run campaigns across social, email, content and web, choosing the channel mix based on the client’s goal
  • Come up with creative concepts from a blank page
  • Work independently by default, and collaborate with designers, writers and other teammates when the project calls for it
  • Make sure every campaign ladders back to data, with a clear metric defined before it launches
  • Work with our analytics lead so content and campaigns support data-driven discovery

Content & Editing

  • Edit AI-assisted and writer drafts (emails, articles, website copy, social) until they meet our quality bar
  • Fact-check and stand behind everything you send to a client
  • Bring specificity, voice and structure to copy

Performance & Reporting

  • Report on progress against each client’s goals
  • Prepare weekly client decks and updates
  • Lead with the “so what”: what happened, why it matters, and what we do next
  • Use what’s working to decide where to double down, adjust or stop
  • Run tests and share what you learned

Client & Team Communication

  • Run day-to-day work with clients alongside our Marketing Manager
  • Present plans, updates and recommendations clearly and confidently
  • Flag risks, blockers and uncertainty early, even before you have the answer
  • Close loops in Asana and in conversation

Systems & Process

  • Manage your own workstreams in Asana
  • Turn lessons learned into templates, SOPs and repeatable workflows

Who You Are

  • 4–6 years of marketing experience, with at least 3 years at an agency handling multiple clients at once
  • A generalist with real range across channels, and curious enough to learn something new when a client needs it
  • Quick to get up to speed on a new industry. You can get credible on enterprise software one week and a cultural institution the next
  • A creative thinker. You can come up with original concepts, not just polish existing ones
  • An editor with taste. You can turn a flat draft into something specific and readable
  • An owner. You define success before you start, make calls with imperfect information, and don’t wait to be told what’s next
  • Focused on results. You balance brand storytelling with growth, and you care whether the work worked, not just that it shipped
  • Coachable. When you get feedback, it shows up in the next version
  • Careful with risk. When something touches budget, timelines, accuracy or the client relationship, you pause and flag it before saying yes
  • Clear and direct. You say “my recommendation is,” and you can disagree well, with clients and with us
  • Comfortable with AI tools, and clear that you’re responsible for what they produce

Bonus Points If…

  • You have strong social instincts and can show us an account you grew or posts you came up with
  • You have experience with short-form video or motion
  • You’ve launched early-stage products or worked closely with product designers and engineers
  • You’ve worked in regulated or compliance-heavy categories
  • You’ve run email programs (Mailchimp a plus)
  • You’ve supported influencer or creator programs

Who This Is Not For

  • Specialists who want to stay in one channel
  • Writers who want to focus mainly on drafting
  • Coordinators who prefer to execute someone else’s plan
  • Candidates without agency experience

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 days: You know your clients, our team and our workflows, and you’re running recurring work on your accounts.
  • 60 days: You’re setting goals and weekly priorities for your accounts without being asked.
  • 90 days: Clients come to you for direction, your drafts need less editing, and your accounts have clear goals with visible progress against them.

Why Work at Big Human?

We believe work is important, but so is taking care of yourself, connecting with your team and stepping away from the screen to recharge. Here are just a few of the perks of working at Big Human:

  • Remote office (with regular coworking days)
  • Health, dental and vision insurance (including an option fully covered by Big Human)
  • 14 paid holidays and generous vacation time
  • 401(k) matching
  • 10–16 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Internet credit and home office upgrade stipend
  • Summer Fridays
  • Yearly team retreat and company-sponsored team events
  • Shared Experience Fund and donation matching
  • Education Fund for professional development

This role is fully remote, with a strong preference for someone based in the Tri-State area (or who can easily travel to NYC for coworking days and team gatherings). Compensation is commensurate with experience and ranges from $85,000–$95,000, depending on background.

Our Values at Big Human

How we work, who we hire and what we build are shaped by our values:

  • We’re supportive. We foster a workplace that encourages creativity, mental wellness and work-life balance.
  • We’re grounded. We think big but stay realistic, humble and ego-free.
  • We’re passionate. We bring commitment, excitement and craft to every project, client or internal.
  • We’re forward-thinking. We build for today while preparing for what’s next.
  • We’re accountable. We show up as individuals and deliver as a team.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

Big Human is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage BIPOC candidates and people from traditionally underrepresented backgrounds to apply. Diverse perspectives fuel creativity and innovation, helping us build better products, brands and experiences.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, veteran status or any other status protected by law.

jobs.title: Freelance Recruiter – Commission Only (€400–2,400 per placement) – Quezon City
jobs.excerpt: European roles, your afternoon hours.  No night shift.
jobs.description:
European roles, your afternoon hours. No night shift. If you recruit for foreign clients from the Philippines, this is the same game, paid per placement in euros. Open to recruiters based in Quezon City and across the Philippines.

Please read the whole post before applying. It's long on purpose. If it isn't for you, that's completely fine, and it saves us both time.

Who we are

BC Recruitment places people in jobs across Europe: multilingual customer service, sales and support roles with some of the biggest international employers, in cities like Athens, Lisbon, Porto, Braga and Sofia. Many of these jobs come with relocation help, which makes them easier to sell to candidates.

We have around 60 open roles right now, in Dutch, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Polish, Turkish, the Nordic languages and more. Alongside those we have specialist roles, like compliance, legal and tech, that pay a lot more per placement.

You don't need to speak the candidates' languages. Every role needs English, and English is what we work in. What matters is that you know where to find people and how to get them excited about a job abroad.

Who we're looking for

People who are hungry, driven and excited about this opportunity, and who believe they can earn more on commission than they do now.

We don't care how many years you've been recruiting. Someone with 6 months of hunger can beat someone with 10 years of experience. We care about what you have personally delivered: how many placements, for what kind of roles, and how many a month.

You'll probably fit if:

  • You've done global or international recruitment, ideally for similar companies or the same kind of candidates: customer service, call centres, multilingual roles, relocation, tourism, hospitality.
  • You're a natural seller who finds people on your own, without leads or hand-holding.
  • You understand that every nationality is found differently. If one channel doesn't work for a market, you know where those people really are and go there.
  • You already have your own tools: LinkedIn, laptop, phone, and whatever else you use to recruit.
  • You want freedom: your own hours, your own place, your own methods, no boss.
  • You have real numbers: placements or sales you made yourself, and you know your monthly average.

This is NOT for you if

  • You want something to try "when you have time".
  • You need someone to tell you what to do every day.
  • You'll blame others when a client pauses a role or a candidate drops out. That's part of recruitment.
  • Most of the people you can reach need a visa. Most of our roles require candidates who can already work in the EU, and we don't offer visa support on most jobs.
  • You need a fixed income soon. There is no salary, retainer or paid trial at the start.
  • You need us to pay for tools before you can work. We don't cover anything at the start.

What you earn

  • Minimum €400 per placement. Most roles pay €400–750, and specialist roles up to €2,400.
  • You see the exact payout on every role before you work on it.
  • A placement counts once your candidate has started and the employer has paid us. Someone who accepts and then drops out is not a placement.
  • Payment usually comes 1–3 months after your candidate starts, depending on the employer. We pay by bank transfer or whatever works for you.
  • Money you've earned is always paid. We know many recruiters are afraid of not being paid. Think about it from our side: a recruiter who delivers is worth far more to us over time than any single placement. This whole system is built on trust, and we'd lose by breaking it.

If you deliver, we deliver back

Nothing is given up front. For proven partners, things grow with your results, agreed case by case:

  • Once you deliver, we cover tool costs such as monthly subscriptions.
  • Proven recruiters can get earlier payouts, arranged with you.
  • Consistent performers can earn a monthly base on top of commission.

The rules bend toward the people who prove themselves. This job gets better the more you deliver.

What you get from day one

  • Proper onboarding: we explain everything, the employers, the roles and how we work, and answer all your questions before you start, so you begin with confidence.
  • Full role details and answers to the questions candidates usually ask.
  • You can reach us directly with any question about a role or a candidate.
  • Total freedom over how, when and where you work.

What's realistic

  • The first weeks are about building your pipeline.
  • Once you're up and running, a below-average recruiter makes about 1 placement a month, a good recruiter 2–5, and our best recruiters 5–10. It gets easier over time: you build a pool of candidates to come back to, and people start recommending you.
  • We expect at least one placement a month once you're up and running.

How we choose

  1. You answer the questions below. We read every answer.
  2. If your answers are strong, we have a video call.
  3. If we're a fit, we onboard you.

Everyone starts with a 30-day trial. Show real progress in that month, with candidates submitted and in interviews, and you stay and grow. If not, we part ways with no hard feelings.

To apply, answer these questions

  1. Your numbers. How many placements have you made per month on average, and for which roles and countries? What was your best month?
  2. The task. We have a Dutch-speaking customer service role in Athens, and candidates must already be allowed to work in the EU. Where exactly would you find 5 of them within two weeks, and how? Name the real channels, groups or searches you'd use.
  3. Commission. Why do you prefer being paid per placement over a salary, or over how you've been paid before?
  4. Your setup. Which tools and channels do you use today? How many hours a week can you put in, and what else are you working on right now?

Apply here with your CV. Then email your answers to , with your name and country in the subject. Applications without answers aren't reviewed.

Optional: attach a voice note or video answering "Why should we pick you?" It's the quickest way for us to get to know you.

Be specific: numbers, names, real examples. Answers that sound AI-written, or that just say what you think we want to hear, are rejected.

You will work at the intersection of technical support, workflow automation, applied AI, analytics, and operational design to streamline how support work is routed, investigated, escalated, synthesized, and improved, with the direct goal of improving customer experience and satisfaction.

What You Will Do

You will build operations intelligence workflows that help Seeq’s Technical Support team act earlier, faster, and with better judgment.

You will work closely with Technical Support Engineers, Support leadership, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to understand how support works across regions, time zones, and escalation paths, then turn those insights into systems that improve the operation.

This role is heavily focused on agentic AI engineering. You will design and implement workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and accelerate high-value support work across ticket triage, routing, knowledge retrieval, escalation preparation, case summarization, data gathering, and root-cause-oriented investigation.

Examples of systems you may build or extend include:

  • AI-assisted ticket triage and routing
  • case summarization and escalation preparation tools
  • knowledge retrieval workflows for support engineers
  • operational insights from ticket patterns, response trends, and escalation signals

You understand that excellent support operations are about improving real workflows such as issue intake, customer communication, troubleshooting, handoffs, backlog management, and trend detection. You turn analysis into recommended actions for Support, Engineering, Product, and Customer Success.

You will translate operational data into actionable intelligence, including support tickets, product usage context, case metadata, response patterns, escalation signals, and internal knowledge sources, delivering the right insights to the right people at the right time.

You know how to apply modern AI and software tooling with rigor and judgment. You can identify where agentic systems genuinely improve throughput and quality, where deterministic automation is better, and how to combine the two safely in production support workflows.

You will also help shape how Seeq operates in an AI-assisted world by creating systems, prompts, tooling, documentation, and conventions that make support workflows easier to execute correctly and easier to improve over time.

You are strong in written communication. You can create documentation, playbooks, prompts, and operating conventions that help other teams adopt what you build and use it well.

You bring strong ownership and agency. You analyze trends, identify friction, quantify opportunity, make sound tradeoffs, and carry improvements through to production and operational adoption.

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.

The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Risk Management

  • Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.
  • Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.
  • Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.

Credit Risk Management

    • Mortgages
    • Personal Loans
    • Credit Cards
    • Auto Loans
    • Consumer Finance Products

Operational Risk Management

Market & Liquidity Risk Oversight

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Are you a high-achieving sales professional ready to digitally transform the physical operations that power our planet? Samsara is seeking a driven Enterprise (Core) Account Executive to introduce our cutting-edge Connected Operations® Platform to Enterprise-sized customers across the UK. This is a unique opportunity to sell a much-needed product into a historically underserved market, working directly with leaders to drive real-world impact and unlock significant career progression. As a Strategic AE you will be helping large mid-market and enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
  • Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Proven expertise winning new business logos through a repeatable sales motion
  • Demonstrable expertise in strategic outbound prospecting, particularly via inside sales
  • Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in Enterprise level accounts, winning multiple $100k+ ARR transactions
  • Experience handling enterprise deal sizes with multiple stakeholders at C-Level
  • Value based selling approach
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, with demonstrated ability thriving in a dynamic, fast-paced environment
  • Working remotely in UK, however comfortable traveling to meet customers as needed

An ideal candidate also has:

  • SaaS sales experience
  • Experience working with line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
  • Comfortable in a dynamic, customer facing environment
  • MEDDIC experience or similar (Sandler Pain Funnel, etc)
  • Excited about solving new problems in innovative ways
  • Highly collaborative with a growth mindset.
  • Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)
  • Passion for the world of operations!

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a hands-on Partnerships & BD expert to grow our banking, deposits, and investing partners, and to bring on the ones we haven't met yet. Most of the job, roughly 70 to 80 percent, is growing the partners we already have: bigger budgets, better economics, broader distribution. The rest is net new, mostly warm, with real outreach on the investing side where the relationships don't exist yet.

You'll work alongside our Head of Partnerships, who will continue to focus on our largest strategic partners. On those strategic partners, you'll run the operations. Across the rest of banking, deposits, and investing, you own it fully, operationally and strategically. That's what gives the Head of Partnerships room for the biggest bets, and it's what makes this seat yours.

This isn't a support role, and it isn't customer service. The job is to grow relationships, not just service them.

WHY THIS SEAT

  • A category to own. Banking, deposits, and investing partners outside our largest strategic accounts are yours, start to finish.
  • A partner, not a handoff. Our Head of Partnerships works closely alongside you for your first 90 days, and the goal is full independence by about day 120.
  • Room to shape it. You'll inherit real momentum, but the strategy in these categories is still being written, and you'll help write it.
  • Close to the media. You'll connect what partners need to placements across FinanceBuzz and our publisher network, which is where a good partnership becomes an extraordinary one.
  • Direct exposure to senior leadership on the deals that matter.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • Direct experience on the advertiser side of a financial comparison publisher, marketplace, or performance network, managing bank, deposit, or investing partners.

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.

The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Risk Management

  • Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.
  • Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.
  • Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.
  • Provide independent oversight of business decisions and strategic initiatives.
  • Promote a strong risk culture throughout the organization.

Credit Risk Management

  • Oversee retail credit portfolios, including:
    • Mortgages
    • Personal Loans
    • Credit Cards
    • Auto Loans
    • Consumer Finance Products
  • Establish underwriting standards and credit policies.
  • Monitor portfolio quality, delinquency trends, and loss performance.
  • Lead stress testing and credit risk scenario analyses.

Job Type: Full-Time, Salaried / Exempt - $120,000 - $140,000

Beyond base salary, we offer competitive health, dental, 401k, and wellness benefits beginning on the first day of employment. This role also is eligible to participate in Kodiak's annual discretionary bonus program, which is dependent on various factors, including individual and company performance.

Kodiak is looking for a seasoned CPG sales leader to accelerate profitable growth across our Midwest / East regional grocery accounts. In this senior individual-contributor role, you will own complex headquarters-level retailer partnerships, shape multi-year customer strategies, and translate category opportunities into stronger distribution, shelf presence, and financial performance. You will lead high-stakes buyer conversations, manage trade investment with discipline, and bring a clear point of view on where Kodiak can win.

***A note about the experience we're seeking: We're looking for someone who has successfully managed grocery retail accounts at the headquarters level, building direct relationships with buyers and category managers to drive sales and growth. While experience in territory sales, district management, direct store delivery, merchandising, and broker representation can provide a great foundation, those backgrounds alone do not fulfill the requirements of this role.

What will you do?

  • Own and expand strategic headquarters-level relationships with Midwest / East regional grocery chains, including senior buyer and category-management stakeholders; serve as the accountable commercial lead for assigned accounts.
  • Build and lead multi-year retailer growth strategies and annual joint business plans, balancing revenue, volume, distribution, margin, and long-term brand-building objectives.
  • Lead complex negotiations on assortment, pricing, promotion, innovation placement, and distribution expansion; create commercially sound solutions that deliver value for Kodiak and retail partners.
  • Own customer-level financial performance, trade investment, and promotional strategy; evaluate spending efficiency, profitability, and return on investment, and make timely course corrections.
  • Drive rigorous account forecasting and business reviews, synthesizing retailer signals, syndicated data, shipment and consumption trends, and promotional plans into actionable projections.
  • Identify whitespace opportunities and create persuasive, category-led growth stories that win shelf space, unlock innovation, and strengthen Kodiak’s competitive position.
  • Direct broker and cross-functional execution across Sales, Finance, Marketing, Shopper Marketing, Supply Chain, and Sales Operations; remove obstacles and ensure commitments translate into results.
  • Anticipate retailer and business risks, lead resolution of complex customer issues, and share account insights and effective practices that elevate the broader sales organization.

You will bring the following capabilities to the role:

  • Strategic headquarters-level selling: Ability to build influential buyer relationships and lead complex, high-value negotiations with regional grocery headquarters.
  • Enterprise-minded account ownership: Ability to connect customer plans to Kodiak’s broader growth, profitability, and category priorities.
  • Advanced commercial and financial judgment: Confidence owning trade budgets, forecasts, customer profitability, promotional ROI, and difficult investment tradeoffs.
  • Category-led influence: Ability to turn consumer, shopper, retailer, and syndicated insights into persuasive recommendations and measurable growth.
  • Senior-level cross-functional leadership: Ability to align stakeholders, direct broker execution, and influence decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • Independent execution and prioritization: Sound judgment and resilience in a remote environment with multiple complex customer priorities.


Your experience should clearly demonstrate:

  • A sustained record of directly owning headquarters-level sales relationships with regional grocery chains in CPG, including independent buyer negotiations and retailer business planning.
  • Experience managing complex or strategically important grocery accounts with clear accountability for revenue, distribution, trade spending, forecasting, and profitability outcomes.
  • Demonstrated success winning incremental distribution, improving customer economics, or growing underperforming accounts through data-backed commercial strategies.
  • Hands-on ownership of annual customer plans, promotional investment decisions, forecast accuracy, and customer-facing business reviews.
  • Ability to use Excel, presentations, syndicated data, and retailer reporting to influence decisions and communicate with senior stakeholders.
  • Experience guiding brokers and cross-functional partners through challenging customer initiatives; experience coaching peers or sharing best practices is valuable but direct people management is not assumed.
  • Ability to travel up to 30% and work effectively in a fully remote environment.

You will turn partner requirements into secure, reliable deployments and sustained operational support, with a strong focus on federal, government, and national security programs.

You will work with a dedicated team of full-stack software engineers and DevOps/SRE engineers, partnering closely with Trase Platform Engineering, Product, GRC, and RCF/RCP technical leaders. The Senior Director, Global Investigator Grants is the senior leader accountable for the strategy, governance, and performance of Precision's global investigator grants and site payment organization. Reporting directly to the VP, Operational Finance, this role leads the Global Investigator Grants team across all regions, ensuring investigator payments, prepaid fund management, forecasting, accruals, and reconciliations are delivered accurately, on time, and in compliance with Clinical Trial Agreements (CTAs), sponsor contracts, and applicable regulations.

The Senior Director leads the integration of acquired and partner site networks into Precision's investigator grants operating model and is accountable for the overall integration of the site payment process within the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS). As a partner to Clinical Operations, Project Management, Site Contracts, Finance, Information Technology, and sponsors, the role builds scalable processes, strong financial controls, and a sponsor experience grounded in transparency, predictability, and audit readiness.

Main Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Global Investigator Grants organization across all regions, setting the strategic vision, operating model, and multi-year roadmap in alignment with Operational Finance and Clinical Solutions objectives.
  • Lead, develop, and retain a global team of an Associate Director, managers, financial analysts – grants and investigator grants associates, including workforce planning and resource allocation to support portfolio growth.
  • Lead the integration of acquired and partner site networks into Precision's investigator grants model, including assessment of existing site payment practices, harmonization of processes, systems, and controls, transition of open site payment obligations and prepaid balances, and post-integration performance monitoring.
  • Serve as the accountable owner for the overall integration of the site payment process within the CTMS, including requirements definition, configuration, data migration, validation, user acceptance testing, go-live readiness, user adoption, and ongoing optimization in partnership with Information Technology, Business Systems, Clinical Operations, and Finance.
  • Establish global governance, policies, SOPs, and financial controls for investigator payments, prepaid fund management, accruals, reconciliations, aggregate spend and transparency reporting (e.g., Sunshine Act), and study closeout to ensure audit and inspection readiness.
  • Provide oversight of investigator grant budgets, forecasting, and accruals across the portfolio, including grant budget impacts within change orders, and report on performance, risks, and prepaid fund positions to the VP, Operational Finance and senior leadership.
  • Serve as the senior escalation point and trusted advisor to sponsors, site networks, and internal leadership on complex grant administration, site payment, contractual, and compliance matters, and participate in executive sponsor meetings and Quarterly Business Reviews.
  • Partner with Business Development, Proposals, and Contracts to shape investigator grant and site payment strategy within proposals, bid defenses, and contract terms, including advance and prepaid funding structures and fair market value approach.
  • Define and monitor global KPIs, service levels, and executive dashboards (e.g., payment cycle times, prepaid fund coverage, forecast accuracy, site satisfaction), and drive continuous improvement, automation, and organizational change management.

Minimum Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated experience leading a clinical systems implementation (CTMS or site payment platform) and/or the integration of acquired operations.

Preferred Education & Experience (optional):

  • MBA, PMP, or equivalent advanced degree or professional certification preferred.
  • Experience integrating site networks or acquired businesses into a global operating model required.
  • Hands-on experience with Veeva Vault Clinical (CTMS and Clinical Finance), Medidata Rave Grants Manager, and ERP/PSA platforms.

Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:

  • Executive Leadership and Vision – Sets strategy and leads a global function through managers and directors, aligning investigator grants operations with Operational Finance, Clinical Solutions, and corporate growth objectives.
  • Integration Leadership – Proven ability to assess, plan, and execute the integration of site networks or acquired operations, harmonizing processes, systems, data, and controls with minimal disruption to sites and sponsors.
  • Clinical Systems Transformation – Deep expertise leading CTMS and site payment system implementations, including requirements, configuration, data migration, validation, and adoption.
  • Global Investigator Grants Expertise – Expert knowledge of CTAs, site budgets, fair market value, payment triggers, prepaid funds, multi-currency payments, and country-specific tax and regulatory requirements.
  • Financial Acumen – Strong command of forecasting, accruals, pass-through cost management, change order impacts, and cash management across a global portfolio.
  • Governance, Compliance and Risk Management – Builds and sustains robust financial controls, SOPs, and audit-ready processes, including aggregate spend and transparency reporting obligations.
  • People Leadership and Talent Development – Develops leaders, builds succession, and fosters a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence across geographies.
  • Sponsor and Stakeholder Influence – Establishes trusted executive relationships with sponsors, site networks, and cross-functional leaders, and influences outcomes without direct authority.
  • Change Management and Continuous Improvement – Leads organizational change, process standardization, and automation initiatives that deliver measurable gains in quality, efficiency, and scalability.

jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Infrastructure Acquisition Group

The Infrastructure Acquisition Group secures the land, power, and data center capacity that enables the Nebius AI Cloud. We identify where Nebius should grow next, structure the commercial agreements that make that growth possible, and partner across engineering, energy, finance, legal, and development to bring new AI infrastructure online.

We're a small, founding team building this function from the ground up across the Americas, leading the acquisition of colocation, build-to-suit, powered land, and other strategic infrastructure opportunities as one of the world's fastest-growing AI cloud platforms scales.

Examples of Problems We're Solving

Validate electrical feasibility before commercial commitment. A site or agreement is only as good as its ability to support the power capacity and distribution infrastructure required to run it. You'll lead electrical due diligence, utility interconnection analysis, and equipment feasibility review to inform Go / No-Go decisions before deals close.

Keep electrical design decisions ahead of development. Coordinate with Site Selection, Development, Engineering, and Delivery so power distribution topology, redundancy strategy, and equipment assumptions are validated early enough to protect schedule and budget once construction begins.

Build a repeatable technical evaluation program. Help establish the standards, design criteria, and technical readiness gates that will support electrical engineering review across every AI infrastructure acquisition in the Americas.

About the Role

As an Electrical Engineer, you'll provide the technical electrical engineering perspective across the acquisition and development lifecycle — from initial site and deal evaluation through construction readiness. Working within the Infrastructure Acquisition Group, you'll partner with Site Selection, Technical Due Diligence, Development, Energy, Finance, and Delivery to ensure every project's power distribution, utility interconnection, and equipment assumptions are technically sound before they move forward.

This is a build-phase role on a build-phase team. Many of the technical evaluation standards, design criteria, and readiness gates you'll use are still being written — in some cases, you'll help write them. We're looking for someone who can independently assess complex electrical infrastructure while helping build the systems that make every future evaluation faster, more predictable, and more scalable.

What You'll Own

  • Lead electrical engineering evaluation of prospective sites, colocation capacity, and build-to-suit opportunities.
  • Own technical assumptions for power distribution topology, capacity, and equipment strategy feeding the pre-construction risk register.
  • Assess utility interconnection, on-site generation, and redundancy strategies (N, N+1, 2N) against site conditions and load requirements.
  • Recommend Go / No-Go input on electrical feasibility as projects advance through key development milestones.
  • Deliver technically validated electrical scope to the Delivery organization with complete documentation and minimized risk.

Technical Due Diligence & Feasibility

  • Lead electrical due diligence on prospective sites, existing facilities, and colocation capacity under evaluation.
  • Evaluate utility capacity, interconnection queue position, substation requirements, and on-site generation/UPS strategy against projected IT load.
  • Assess electrical equipment availability, lead times (transformers, switchgear, generators), and vendor constraints that could affect schedule or capex.
  • Ensure electrical assumptions are fully integrated into project budgets, capacity models, and schedules.

Design & Equipment Strategy

  • Partner with Engineering to define power distribution topology and redundancy strategy appropriate to each site and deal structure.
  • Evaluate EPMS/BMS controls integration and electrical system commissioning requirements early in the acquisition process.
  • Provide technical input on switchgear, UPS, and generator selection, redundancy strategy, and capex trade-offs across candidate sites.
  • Ensure electrical design intent is preserved as deals move from negotiation into development.

Construction Readiness

  • Establish electrical technical readiness criteria as part of project handoff standards.
  • Verify electrical design assumptions, equipment specifications, and capacity commitments are complete before turnover to Delivery.
  • Identify and resolve electrical technical risks before they impact construction.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Serve as the primary electrical engineering technical interface across Site Selection, Technical Due Diligence, Development, Energy, and Delivery.
  • Coordinate with consulting engineers, utility providers, equipment vendors, and commissioning agents to validate executable electrical strategies.
  • Align internal stakeholders and external consultants to prevent technical scope drift as projects move from acquisition into development.

What Success Looks Like

  • Ensure every acquisition is grounded in sound electrical engineering judgment before commercial commitment.
  • Deliver predictable, technically validated power distribution and redundancy strategies across the portfolio.
  • Identify and resolve electrical technical risks before they impact construction.
  • Build trusted relationships with utility providers, equipment vendors, consulting engineers, and commissioning partners.
  • Help build the technical standards and evaluation processes the Infrastructure Acquisition Group runs on as it scales.

What You'll Bring

  • You're comfortable operating in ambiguity and building technical evaluation processes where none exist. You know how to independently assess complex electrical infrastructure while helping define how future projects should be evaluated.
  • 8+ years of experience in data center electrical engineering, power systems design, or mission-critical electrical systems.
  • Experience with medium-voltage distribution, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, and utility interconnection for high-density AI/hyperscale environments.
  • Strong understanding of electrical capacity planning, redundancy topology (N, N+1, 2N), equipment selection, and capex trade-offs in data center design.
  • Experience evaluating electrical feasibility of sites or facilities prior to commercial commitment.
  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center or AI infrastructure development.
  • Experience with EPMS/BMS controls integration and electrical systems commissioning.
  • Experience with utility interconnection agreements and interconnection queue strategy.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or similar professional certification.
  • Experience evaluating colocation or build-to-suit electrical infrastructure in a due diligence capacity.

Why Join Nebius

The infrastructure supporting AI is being built now. This is an opportunity to help define how Nebius evaluates and designs the power systems behind every AI infrastructure acquisition while helping build the function itself — the technical standards, design criteria, and evaluation framework that will support infrastructure investments across the Americas. You'll work on some of the industry's largest and most complex AI infrastructure developments while helping shape the physical foundation of the global AI economy.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

In this role you will design and build learning from start to finish: on-demand modules, microlearning, learning paths, scenario-based simulations, interactive stories, video, podcasts, manipulatives for live training, and audio, etc working directly with portfolio managers and subject matter experts. In the first year, the defining work is building reusable design patterns and content standards that make our learning consistent, accessible, and quick to produce with quality and measurable impact.


What We’re Looking For


A learning designer first. You design for outcomes and behavior change, not seat time.

A maker. You have a portfolio of shipped digital learning, simulations, or multi-media and the technical skills to build it.

A strong writer. You make complex ideas clear, and your content reads as though it was written for the learner.

AI curious and hands-on. You use AI to work faster and better, and you hold a high bar for quality and accuracy.

A collaborator. You partner easily with SMEs and U.S.-based business colleagues, give and receive critique, and deliver on time.


Responsibilities


Design and build learning

  • Design and build on-demand courses, microlearning, learning paths, and in-the-flow resources that are easy to find, start, and finish.
  • Design simulations, scenario-based learning, and gamified experiences that build skills through realistic practice and feedback.

Produce your own assets

  • Build and produce your own learning assets from start to finish, including e-learning modules in authoring tools like Articulate Storyline or Rise, scripted and edited videos, screen recordings, audio, graphics, and animations, and package them for LMS deployment.
  • Write clear, accessible, on-brand content such as scripts, job aids, and guides.

Partner with the business

  • Work with SMEs and portfolio managers in U.S. working hours to turn expertise into practical content, and know when a simpler approach will do.
  • Define measures of success up front and work with Learning Measurement to evaluate effectiveness.

Set standards and patterns

  • Develop reusable templates, design patterns, and content standards (including xAPI and accessibility requirements) with the studio and Learning Operations.
  • Handle business content responsibly, using fictional or de-identified data in examples and following confidentiality and brand guidelines.

Reimagine production with AI

  • Use AI to accelerate scripting, storyboarding, asset creation, localization, and updating content, directing it toward your own design vision. You own the outcome, including its accuracy.

What You Own


Digital Products

  • On-demand and microlearning
  • Learning paths
  • In-the-flow resources
  • Product improvement

Immersive & Media

  • Simulations and scenarios
  • Video, audio, and animation
  • Interactive stories
  • Accessible, on-brand assets

Standards & Craft

  • Templates and design patterns
  • xAPI and accessibility
  • AI-enabled production
  • Peer critique

Education and Skills

  • 7+ years in instructional or learning experience design, digital content creation, or interactive media production.
  • 3+ years of experience in a management capacity highly preferred.
  • Portfolio demonstrating digital learning products, simulations, or rich multi-media learning with measurable results.
  • Proficiency with authoring and media tools (e.g., Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Creative Cloud) and an understanding of LMS, xAPI, and accessibility standards.
  • Experience applying user-centered design and iterating based on data.
  • Fluency in English required; Spanish is a plus. Ability to work U.S. business hours.
  • Desirable: experience using generative AI in content production.

What Success Looks Like

  • Cencora University can increasingly say: Our learning is well made, easy to use, and worth coming back to.
  • Digital and immersive learning follows one set of design and content standards and is visibly on-brand.
  • Time to create and refresh content has dropped as AI-assisted workflows take hold.

Success isn’t more courses. Success is learning people use and performance that changes.

jobs.description:
Corporate Travel Consultant (Truist Team)

FCM takes a holistic approach to corporate travel, specializing in managing national and global travel programs for medium and large businesses.

Ranked as one of the world’s top five travel management companies, it has a business network in over 97 countries and global headquarters in London, Brisbane, Singapore and New York. Backed by the global strength of Flight Centre Travel Group (FCTG), FCM combines local expertise and global experience to provide clients with a truly bespoke experience.

To learn more about FCM please click HERE

About the Opportunity

This role will have you arranging domestic and complex international travel for busy executives including air, car hotel and ground transportation. Before you begin your role, you will spend four weeks (paid) training. This program will boost your knowledge, train you on contract airfares and sharpen your Sabre skills. Our corporate travel agents handle the air, car, rail and ground transportation bookings as well as the ticketing, changes and the exchange and queue management.  You will also need to offer exceptional customer service to satisfy our business traveler’s needs. We encourage our Corporate Travel Agents to study the travel polices of our corporate accounts and develop a relationship with them so when our valued business travelers have the need for business travel arrangements, they rest assured that their business travel needs are in the hands of a dedicated team of Corporate Travel professionals they trust and are on a first name basis with.

Our business hours are 8:00 AM AM to 8:00 PM EST Monday – Friday.

A typical schedule will include a 40-hour work week with five 8-hour shifts. Be prepared to work an evening shift until 8:00 PM once or twice a week.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate air, hotel, car, and ground transportation bookings for domestic and international travel
  • Build rapport and develop a relationship with business travelers to ensure their business travel needs are in the hands of a trusted team of Corporate Travel professionals
  • Ensure accurate and timely completion of reservations while meeting travelers' needs
  • Executing all responsibilities within company guidelines for customer service, documentation of PNRS (Passenger Name Records) and profiles, ticketing, invoicing, and maintaining accuracy throughout
  • Staying fully informed about airline rules, regulations, tariffs, and fare requirements and applying this knowledge accurately to all travel arrangements
  • Deliver consultative support and exceptional customer service throughout the booking process
  • Keeping clients informed about all necessary travel documents and health requirements for their destinations
  • Proficiently handling ticketing, Phase IVs, and exchanges/changes involving complex international fares
  • Expertly managing rerouting and exchange processes, ensuring minimal disruption to travel plans
  • Other duties and tasks as assigned
  • Contribute to a safe, inclusive, and accessible work environment where all Flighties feel welcomed, respected, and supported to thrive

Experience & Qualifications

  • 2+ years of recent, prior experience in corporate travel management, understanding the unique needs and challenges of business travelers.
  • In-depth familiarity with current Sabre GDS (Global Distribution System) for fare calculations, itinerary management, and ticket issuance.
  • Previous exposure to quality control processes to ensure the accuracy and compliance of travel bookings.
  • Proficiency in ticketing procedures and scripting, along with the ability to handle complex itinerary changes and exchanges for both international and domestic travel.
  • Proven ability to navigate and manipulate complex itineraries, international fares, and Passenger Name Records (PNRs) to meet client requirements.
  • A polished and professional demeanor when interacting with clients and colleagues.
  • Proficiency in handling multiple urgent tasks simultaneously while maintaining efficiency and quality in each interaction.
  • The capacity to make quick and effective decisions to resolve travel-related issues promptly.
  • Excellent communication skills to keep clients informed and reassured throughout the travel process.
  • A deep commitment to delivering exceptional customer service with a focus on client satisfaction.
  • Comfortable and proficient in using travel booking systems and various communication tools.
  • Strong technical aptitude with the ability to troubleshoot and adapt to new technologies
  • Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and manage tasks successfully
  • Reliable, high-speed internet connectivity required to support core job responsibilities, including but not limited to video conferencing, access to company systems, and secure handling of company data.

Work Perks! - What’s in it for you:

FCTG is renowned internationally for having amazing perks and an even better culture. We understand that our people are our most valuable asset. It is the passion and dedication of our teams that keep the company on top of the industry ladder. It’s also why we offer some great employee benefits and perks outside of the norm.

  • Have fun:At the heart of everything we do at Flight Centre is a desire to have fun.
  • Reward & Recognition: Celebrate the success of yourself and others at our regular Buzz Nights and at the annual Global Gathering - You'll have to experience it to believe it!
  • Use your smarts:Our people use their quick thinking, expertise, and tenacity to always figure things out.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

WELLBE INTRODUCTION

The WellBe care model is a Physician Led Advanced Practice geriatric care (care of older adults) team focused on the care of the frail, poly-chronic, elderly Medicare Advantage patients. This population is typically underserved and very challenged with access to care. To address these problems, we have elected to bring the care to the patient, instead of trying to bring the patient to the care. Care is provided throughout the entire continuum of care – from chronic care and urgent care in the home, to hospital, to skilled nursing facility, to assisted living, to palliative care, to end of life care. WellBe's physician/advanced practicing clinician led geriatric care teams’ partner with the patient’s primary care physician to provide concierge level geriatric medical care and social support in the home as well as delivering and coordinating across the entire care continuum.

GENERAL SUMMARY

This role will advance WellBe’s understanding of our patient's healthcare utilization and how we can reduce unnecessary healthcare costs while achieving better patient outcomes, and patient experience. The ideal candidate will have a solid knowledge/understanding of healthcare data sets, including medical claims, HCC, HEDIS, Eligibility and Census. This role reports to the Manager of Data and Quality Management and works closely with operational and clinical leaders. The HealthCare Reporting Analyst will be responsible for collecting, preparing, and acting upon data to ensure data integrity. This role will give you the opportunity to use your analytical knowledge and skill to derive insights which will drive actions and generate value from that intelligence by initiating new analytic solutions and by providing input to operations processes.

We are looking for a digital native with a curious and inventive mind, obsessive attention to detail, and an instinctive understanding of how to explore, understand and communicate data; someone who appreciates the importance of clarity, simplicity and has the creativity to envision outstanding user experiences and the discipline to make them real. A wonderful opportunity to be part of an incredible team who work tirelessly to provide concierge level medical care to an often-underserved community.

Job Description

SKILLS & COMPETENCIES

  • Responsible for analytic data needs of various business unit
  • Handle complex data projects and acts as a lead for other Data Analysts
  • Daily administration and proactive monitoring of business-critical data in integrated databases
  • Manage process queues and mitigate any exception output within expected SLAs
  • Manage the quality of data processed through health plan and partner submitted data sources
  • Perform accuracy checks and resolve exceptions produced by integration processes
  • Provide data stewardship and governance for business operations in all or some of the following areas: claims, provider data, member data, clinical data, HEDIS, pharmacy, external reporting
  • Review data to determine operational impacts and needed actions; elevate issues, trends, areas for improvement and opportunities to management.
  • Develop reports and deliverables for management
  • Create data dictionaries to document data types, associated business rules, and remediations paths
  • Test and correct errors, and refine changes to database
  • Perform end to end diagnostic analytics to identify data anomalies to be resolved and fixed at source
  • Assist with training and mentoring other Data Analysts.
  • Work with key business owners to establish and meet their data needs and the data needs of the organization
  • Work with IT and Analytics teams to operationalize analytic and reporting innovations
  • Other tasks needed to accomplish team’s objectives/goals
  • Answer user questions
  • Confers with co-workers to determine impact of database changes on other systems

Salary: $70,000 - $141,000/year

Job Requirements

Educational/Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related field or equivalent experience.
  • 4 years of data stewardship or data analysis experience. Healthcare experience required.
  • 2+ years of experience in health care data analysis

Required Skills and Abilities:

  • Advanced knowledge of Enterprise Reporting and Analysis tools, SQL, and visual analytic applications.
  • Proven experience, ideally in healthcare, with Data Governance, Catalog and Data Quality products. Hands-on experience defining data and quality standards and building data integration workflows in a data analyst role.
  • Fluency in SQL or other similar programming languages. Some development experience in at least one scripting language (Python, R, etc.) is a plus.
  • Experience launching internal metric dashboards and scorecards
  • Snowflake experience preferred
  • Computer programming basics to interpret and understand logic/code behind

Work Conditions: Ability to lift up to 20lbs. Moving lifting or transferring of patients may involve lifting of up to 50lbs as well as assist with weights of more than 100lbs.

  • Ability to stand for extended periods
  • Ability to drive to patient locations (ie. home, hospital, SNF, etc)
  • Fine motor skills
  • Visual acuity

Compliance Program Manager

Department / Seat Name: Compliance
Location: Remote (Role is open to only U.S.-based, U.S.-citizen-only)
Salary: $105,000-$145,000
Type: W2; Full-Time

Role Summary
The Compliance Program Manager owns the full lifecycle of compliance frameworks across the
organization, from regulatory monitoring and internal program readiness through to the
productization and launch of new service offerings. This role is the single accountable owner
for knowing what is changing in the regulatory and framework landscape, determining what the
organization must do about it internally, and converting qualifying frameworks into repeatable,
sellable, deliverable service lines.

This is a hybrid compliance and product role. Approximately half the seat is program
management: tracking framework requirements, owning internal compliance obligations,
maintaining authorization and accreditation readiness, and driving remediation to closure. The
other half is product management: business case development, scoping, methodology design,
pricing input, enablement, and launch coordination for new offerings.
The role is not a people management position but carries cross-functional accountability
across PMO, TAC, Sales, RFP, Marketing, and Finance.

Role Purpose
● To ensure the organization is never surprised by a compliance change, never out of
compliance with the frameworks and authorizations it operates under, and never late to
market with a new offering that the changing landscape creates demand for.

Core Responsibilities

● Compliance Program Ownership
● Own the organization-wide compliance framework calendar, tracking rule changes,
standard revisions, program updates, and authorization requirements across all
frameworks the company operates under or delivers against
● Maintain a current obligations register mapping each external requirement to an internal
owner, control, artifact, and evidence location
● Drive internal readiness for new and renewing authorizations, accreditations, and
program approvals, including document production, gap closure, and submission
coordination
● Coordinate internal audits, surveillance activities, and external assessment cycles,
including scheduling, evidence collection, corrective action tracking, and closure
verification
● Track and drive corrective actions, nonconformities, and findings to documented
closure with defined owners and due dates
● Monitor regulatory and standards bodies for changes affecting the organization's
authorizations, delivery methodologies, or service eligibility, and issue timely impact
analyses to leadership
● Maintain the compliance obligations documentation set, ensuring version control,
currency, and traceability
● Serve as the internal subject matter expert on framework requirements, providing
authoritative interpretation to delivery, sales, and leadership teams
● Escalate impartiality, independence, conflict of interest, and eligibility questions to the
appropriate authority rather than resolving them unilaterally

Productization and Offering Ownership
● Evaluate emerging and revised frameworks for market opportunity, producing a written
business case covering demand signal, competitive landscape, required capability,
margin profile, and go/no-go recommendation
● Own the end-to-end productization of approved offerings, including scope definition,
deliverable set, methodology, work breakdown structure, level of effort model, and
quality gates
● Partner with Finance and Sales leadership to develop pricing, rate card entries, and
margin targets for new offerings
● Build and maintain the delivery artifact set for each offering, document templates,
evidence requirements, and reporting formats
● Partner with TAC and delivery leadership to define staffing requirements, required
credentials, and technical readiness for each new offering
● Develop and deliver enablement materials for Sales, RFP, and delivery teams, including
positioning, qualification criteria, and scoping guidance
● Own the launch plan and post-launch review for each new offering
● Maintain the offering portfolio, identifying offerings that should be revised, repriced,
consolidated, or retired
● Partner with Marketing on messaging accuracy and technical claim review for all
compliance-related content

These are tracked weekly or monthly via the Scorecard:
● Percentage of tracked frameworks with a current obligations mapping
● Open corrective actions past due
● Average days to close a corrective action
● Authorization and accreditation milestones met on schedule
● Regulatory change impact analyses issued within the defined SLA
● Number of framework evaluations completed
● Number of offerings launched per quarter against plan
● Days from go decision to first sellable offering

Payroll Management

  • Maintain employee payroll records, timesheets, leave entitlements and payroll adjustments.

  • Ensure payroll practices comply with Australian employment legislation and relevant award requirements.
  • Respond to payroll-related queries and resolve discrepancies.

Bookkeeping & Financial Administration

  • Manage accounts payable, including supplier invoices, payment processing and expense coding.
  • Manage accounts receivable, including customer invoicing, payment allocations and debtor follow-ups.
  • Perform regular bank, credit card and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Maintain accurate general ledger entries and financial records.
  • Process supplier payments, staff reimbursements and other business expenses.
  • Monitor outstanding invoices and assist with cash flow management.

Financial Reporting & Compliance

  • Assist with month-end financial processes and preparation of management reports.
  • Prepare and maintain records for Payroll Tax, GST, BAS, PAYG and other statutory obligations.
  • Assist with BAS preparation and coordinate with external accountants when required.
  • Investigate discrepancies and ensure financial records are complete and accurate.
  • Maintain organized financial documentation for reporting and audit purposes.

Requirements

  • Minimum 1-2 years of experience in payroll and bookkeeping, preferably supporting Australian businesses.
  • Strong knowledge of Australian payroll requirements, including STP, PAYG, superannuation and leave entitlements.
  • Practical experience with GST, BAS, accounts payable, accounts receivable and bank reconciliations.
  • Proficiency in the accounting software Xero.
  • Knowledge of EzzyBills desired.
  • Knowledge of Simpro Software desired.
  • Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial data.
  • Good understanding of Australian taxation and bookkeeping practices.
  • High level of accuracy, organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently, manage deadlines and handle confidential financial information.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Personal Attributes

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented.
  • Trustworthy and comfortable handling sensitive financial information.
  • Proactive in identifying and resolving discrepancies.
  • Able to manage competing priorities and meet payroll deadlines.
  • Reliable, accountable and capable of working with minimal supervision.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset.

This is a remote role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor”)
