About Gruve

Gruve is an innovative software services startup dedicated to transforming enterprises to AI powerhouses. We specialize in cybersecurity, customer experience, cloud infrastructure, and advanced technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs). Our mission is to assist our customers in their business strategies utilizing their data to make more intelligent decisions. As a well-funded early-stage startup, Gruve offers a dynamic environment with strong customer and partner networks.

Position summary:

We are looking for a skilled L2 System Administrator to support Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Microsoft Teams and related collaboration workloads. The role is responsible for incident resolution, service administration, troubleshooting, service health monitoring and configuration management. The administrator will work closely with L1 operations, L3 SMEs, Identity, Security and Network teams to maintain service availability and SLA compliance.

Key Responsibilities:

Exchange Online & Email Operations

  • Provide L2 support for Exchange Online incidents, mail flow issues and service requests.
  • Troubleshoot email delivery failures, mailbox access, shared mailboxes, distribution lists and mail flow rules.
  • Support mailbox permissions, delegation, mailbox configuration and approved administrative changes.
  • Investigate message trace results, mail flow errors and connectivity issues.
  • Support mailbox migration and hybrid Exchange-related operational activities where applicable.

Microsoft Teams & Collaboration

  • Administer and troubleshoot Microsoft Teams, including meeting, messaging, calling and access issues.
  • Support Teams policies, membership, permissions and collaboration settings.
  • Troubleshoot SharePoint Online site access, permissions and document collaboration issues.
  • Support OneDrive synchronization, sharing, access and storage-related incidents.

jobs.excerpt: About the Role: At TELUS Digital, we are teaching AI to move from 2D screens into 3D reality.
jobs.description:
About the Role:

At TELUS Digital, we are teaching AI to move from 2D screens into 3D reality. As a 3D Spatial Data Expert, you are the "Mapmaker of the Future." You will join our AI Community as a specialist tasked with identifying and labeling the physical world within 3D datasets, such as LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) and 3D meshes. While our Specialists handle complex physics and urban planning, you are the one who teaches the AI the "alphabet" of space—where a curb ends, where a pedestrian begins, and how a robotic arm perceives a shelf. At TELUS, you are helping to build the data foundation for autonomous vehicles, drones, and the industrial metaverse.

What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities):

  • 3D Bounding Box Annotation: Placing precise 3D cubes (bounding boxes) around objects in point-cloud data to help AI identify their size, location, and orientation in space.

  • Semantic Segmentation: "Painting" 3D maps to categorize different surfaces—distinguishing between a drivable road, a sidewalk, and a permanent obstacle.

  • Point-Cloud Cleaning: Reviewing raw sensor data from self-driving cars or robots to remove "noise" (like rain or dust) so the AI sees a clear picture of reality.

  • Simulated Data Validation: Comparing AI-generated 3D environments against real-world captures to ensure the digital version is a faithful "twin" of the physical one.

  • Spatial Logic Testing: Answering simple questions about 3D scenes (e.g., "Is the drone's path clear of the overhead wire?") to validate the model's spatial reasoning.

    • Contribute to the optimisation of the company’s website (landing pages, conversion paths)
    • Track and report performance using clear KPI (pipeline contribution, lead quality, channel ROI), not just activity metrics.

​​Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian and US companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines. For this role, you will be engaged directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: A finance and CFO advisory firm providing finance and operational BAU outsourced services and advisory services to growing mid-sized businesses. The firm supports clients with financial management, reporting, analysis, and commercial decision-making through a practical, hands-on approach to improve financial processes and provide actionable growth insights.

Role Overview: We are looking for an experienced and detail-oriented Accountant to support the day-to-day accounting operations of a US-based branch while working Australian hours and collaborating closely with the finance teams in the US and Australia. Key responsibilities include accounts payable, bank and credit card reconciliations, month-end closing, general ledger accounting, and tax compliance support. The successful candidate should be comfortable communicating across time zones, following a structured and repeatable month-end process, and working independently. A structured handover and overlap period will be provided upon joining.

Key Responsibilities:

Accounts Payable and Vendor Management

  • Manage the end-to-end accounts payable process, including invoice review, coding, processing, and posting.
  • Prepare and coordinate vendor payments through online banking platforms.
  • Reconcile vendor statements and investigate outstanding balances or discrepancies.
  • Monitor unpaid invoices and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to ensure timely payments.

Bank and Credit Card Reconciliations

  • Perform regular bank reconciliations and investigate unreconciled transactions.
  • Review and record corporate credit card transactions, ensuring accurate general ledger classifications.
  • Identify and resolve discrepancies between bank records and accounting system balances.
  • Monitor outstanding transactions and follow up on necessary adjustments.

Month-End Closing and General Accounting

  • Prepare and post journal entries, including accruals, reversals, and reclassifications.
  • Review balance sheet accounts and reconcile general ledger balances.
  • Assist with month-end closing activities to ensure timely and accurate financial reporting.
  • Maintain supporting schedules and working papers for assigned accounts.
  • Coordinate intercompany transactions and reconciliations.

Tax and Regulatory Compliance Support

  • Assist external tax consultants by providing accounting records, reports, and supporting documentation as requested.
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders to address inquiries and information requests relating to US sales and use tax and other tax compliance matters.
  • Review and reconcile relevant accounting data to support external tax consultants.

Financial Reporting and Budget Support

  • Assist in preparing financial reports and supporting schedules.
  • Review accounting records for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Support budgeting and financial analysis activities as required.
  • Provide financial information and respond to management inquiries.

Process Improvement and Coordination

  • Identify opportunities to improve accounting workflows and internal controls.
  • Coordinate with finance team members and other departments to resolve accounting issues.
  • Maintain organized and accurate accounting documentation.
  • Handle other accounting and administrative tasks as assigned.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accountancy, Finance, or a related field.
  • CPA qualification is preferred.
  • At least 5 years of relevant accounting experience, with Australian or US accounting experience preferred.
  • Strong experience in accounts payable, bank reconciliations, general ledger accounting, and month-end closing.
  • Experience with Microsoft Dynamics NAV or similar ERP systems is preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and accuracy when handling financial records and transactions.
  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and meet deadlines.
  • Willing to work 6:00 AM to 2:00 PM AEST to ensure sufficient overlap with the US-based finance team.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Experience using US banking platforms for payment processing and reconciliation.
  • Experience in intercompany accounting and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Familiarity with supporting external tax consultants and responding to tax-related information requests.
  • Previous experience working in a multinational or outsourced accounting environment.
  • Ability to manage time-sensitive accounting deliverables while maintaining accuracy and organization.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

After Hours Senior Travel Manager (VIP)

A world where tech and people work collectively to make corporate travel simpler, faster and easier.

Corporate Traveler is one of Flight Centre Travel Group’s (FCTG) most successful brands, globally. Our mission is to dominate the SME market, making the end-to-end travel experience faster, simpler and easier for our customers and to demonstrate ongoing value to decision-makers, travelers and bookers. We provide our customers with the perfect blend of personal, local service blended with our expert technology suite and the great choice and value which comes with being part of the FCTG family. For decades, we’ve been helping go-getter businesses grow through travel.

Corporate Traveler has offices across a global network that spans Australia, Canada, USA, UK, South Africa and New Zealand. The brand has been part of the Flight Centre Travel Group for more than 26 years and is a key contributor to the ongoing strength of FCTG’s corporate travel division. Award winning, forward thinking and fun to work for – this is a business for people who love travel, are team players and customer service oriented.

To learn more about Corporate Traveler please click HERE

About The Opportunity

As a Senior Travel Manager on the After Hours Support Team, you will play a vital leadership role in delivering exceptional travel experiences for VIP corporate clients outside of standard business hours. This position combines operational leadership, coaching, and high-level travel expertise to ensure seamless service delivery during evenings, weekends, holidays, and overnight shifts. You’ll serve as a key resource for consultants and offshore teams while supporting a culture of collaboration, accountability, and premium client service. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and enjoy leading by example while solving complex travel challenges, this is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide training and mentorship for novice Travel Managers and act as an on-shift buddy when assigned.
  • Coordinate and support helper coverage during shifts, particularly on weekends.
  • Post regular Taskmaster updates in designated Teams channels.
  • Serve as Email Captain as assigned and monitor Emailgistics folders.
  • Approve team breaks, lunches, and HOPs.
  • Monitor call and email dashboards to drive productivity and service efficiency.
  • Proactively check in with team members and address workflow challenges.
  • Respond to questions from consultants and offshore support teams.
  • Manage leadership escalations related to active customer service issues.
  • Engage senior leadership when urgent business issues arise.
  • Adjust schedules and coordinate coverage for team callouts.
  • Send urgent alerts when emergency staffing coverage is required.
  • Monitor significant I.T. disruptions and escalate operationally impactful issues.
  • Utilize Sabre GDS, NDC solutions, and web-based booking platforms to arrange accurate VIP corporate travel reservations.
  • Deliver high-touch, white-glove service to executive-level and high-value travelers.
  • Support operational initiatives and special projects as assigned.
  • Contribute to a safe, inclusive, and accessible work environment where all Flighties feel welcomed, respected, and supported to thrive

Experience & Qualifications

  • Minimum 2+ years of experience as an After Hours Travel Manager within Corporate Traveler.
  • Demonstrated leadership, coaching, and training experience.
  • Strong knowledge and practical experience using Sabre GDS.
  • Experience working with NDC and web-based travel booking platforms.
  • Proven ability to support VIP, executive-level, or high-value corporate travelers.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to service excellence.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and perform effectively under pressure.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.
  • Professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment when handling escalations.
  • Flexibility to work a 40-hour schedule that may include weekends, overnights, holidays, and varying shift patterns.
  • Reliable, high-speed internet connectivity required to support core job responsibilities, including but not limited to video conferencing, access to company systems, and secure handling of company data.

Schedule Flexibility: Final team placement and/or shift schedule may be adjusted depending on applicant availability. We are especially interested in candidates open to working late evening hours (until 1–2 AM PST) as an alternative to a full overnight shift.

Work Perks! - What’s in it for you:

FCTG is renowned internationally for having amazing perks and an even better culture. We understand that our people are our most valuable asset. It is the passion and dedication of our teams that keep the company on top of the industry ladder. It’s also why we offer some great employee benefits and perks outside of the norm.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara’s UK Enterprise business is one of our fastest-growing segments globally. We’ve scaled rapidly over the past several years — consistently outpacing the broader business — and we’re now at an inflection point where we need to pair that momentum with operational rigour to sustain growth at scale.

This Regional Sales Director role is central to that next chapter. You’ll lead a team of six Senior Enterprise Account Executives and Client Directors selling into some of the UK’s largest and most complex organisations, spanning transportation, logistics, infrastructure, utilities, and field services.

The team is performing — but we want to turn strong results into a repeatable, scalable engine. That means bringing structure, coaching discipline, and a proven enterprise playbook without losing the pace and builder energy that got us here.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the performance, development, and day-to-day leadership of a team of Senior Enterprise AEs, driving net new logo acquisition and expansion across a defined set of strategic UK accounts
  • Coach your team through complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles where average contract values regularly reach seven figures over multi-year terms
  • Build and run a structured operating rhythm - pipeline reviews, deal inspection, forecasting discipline - while getting close enough to the detail to add value at the deal level
  • Develop your reps’ ability to access economic buyers, build multi-threaded relationships, and position Samsara’s expanding product portfolio against a customer’s most critical business priorities
  • Pressure-test deal qualification, challenge assumptions, and help your team navigate the complexity of selling into large UK enterprises - this isn’t a role where you sit above the deals
  • Build the commercial muscles - cross-sell, multi-product attach, stakeholder mapping - that will drive durable growth as we expand our footprint across the UK’s largest accounts
  • Partner closely with the AVP of Strategic and Enterprise Sales UK, your peer RSDs, and cross-functional teams including Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Marketing to ensure your team has the support it needs to win
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
  • Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Proven experience as a frontline or second-line sales leader in B2B enterprise technology, with direct responsibility for team quota attainment
  • Track record of coaching Account Executives through complex, multi-quarter sales cycles with average deal sizes of £250K+ ACV, but with experience of seven figure ACV deals
  • Experience selling into large, multi-stakeholder organisations where procurement, legal, and multiple business units are involved in the buying decision
  • Demonstrated ability to build and enforce a structured sales operating cadence — pipeline generation, deal qualification, forecasting accuracy, and stage progression
  • Strong commercial instinct for multi-product or platform selling, where the value proposition spans multiple use cases and buyer personas

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience at a high-growth technology company that was scaling its enterprise go-to-market in the UK or EMEA — ideally where you helped build or refine the playbook rather than inheriting an established one
  • A coaching-first leadership style with a track record of developing AEs from good to exceptional, not just managing top performers
  • Experience managing forecast accuracy as a discipline, not just an output — particularly in an environment where leadership investment decisions depend on the reliability of your calls
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, scaling organisation where not everything is perfectly defined yet, and where you’re expected to build process while delivering results
  • A blend of strategic thinking and tactical intensity — you can set a multi-year account strategy and also jump into a deal review and tell a rep exactly where their qualification is weak

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

The role requires a transformational leader who can think strategically, remain technically credible, and stay sufficiently close to execution to challenge teams, vendors and delivery partners.

Cloud and Infrastructure Strategy

  • Define and execute the long-term cloud and infrastructure strategy, roadmap and operating model.

  • Translate future business demand and technology trends into a practical three-to-five-year transformation roadmap.

Transformation and Modernisation

  • Lead large-scale cloud, data centre and infrastructure transformation programmes.
  • Drive cloud adoption, infrastructure modernisation, platform standardisation and enterprise migration initiatives.
  • Establish reusable engineering patterns, platform guardrails and standardised service offerings.
  • Promote self-service provisioning through Infrastructure-as-Code, policy-as-code and automation.

Infrastructure Engineering and Delivery

  • Oversee the design and delivery of cloud landing zones, hybrid hosting platforms and foundational infrastructure.

  • Define engineering standards, reference architectures and reusable infrastructure modules.

Production Operations and Reliability

jobs.description:
About Pragma & FirstLook

Pragma builds software that helps game studios create great games and lasting relationships with their players. FirstLook helps studios run playtests, understand their audiences, and build engaged player communities. Our work connects game developers, players, and creators, with the goal of helping great games find and grow their audiences.

You'll be joining a deeply experienced team who have scaled some of the largest games in the world, including League of Legends and Destiny 2. Our team also brings platform experience from Google, Twitch, Amazon, and Microsoft.

We are a Series B company backed by globally renowned technology investors, including Greylock, Insight Partners, and Upfront Ventures.

Location: Remote, based in Europe or North America

Coverage: Strategic accounts across North America and Europe, with APAC support during overlapping hours

Employment: Part-time hourly contract (up to 20 hours/week) to start, with a path to full time as the program grows

About the role
We’re building a managed services offering for FirstLook, and we’re looking for someone to lead it.

More and more studios see community management as a service they buy, not a role they hire for. Some just need their Discord set up. Others have FirstLook but not the bandwidth or skills to use it fully. Some lose a key person in the middle of a playtest. What they all want is someone who can come in and run it: their FirstLook setup, playtests, player comms, Discord, and sometimes their creator program.

You’ll start by doing this for a small number of studios, working embedded with their teams alongside our customer success and sales teams. As demand grows, you’ll turn the work into packages, templates, and playbooks we can offer studios of every size, from self-serve resources for small teams to fully managed support for publishers.

This role starts as a part-time contract. As the business grows, we expect it to become full time.

What you will do
Run FirstLook and player operations for studios

  • Plan and run playtests end to end in FirstLook, including flows, surveys, NDAs, invite waves, player comms, and follow-up.
  • Write and schedule player communications, track conversion at each step, and adjust to improve results.
  • Turn playtest data, player feedback, and community sentiment into clear readouts for the studio.
  • Coordinate player recruitment with our team, using both our player network and paid acquisition campaigns.

Community management and moderation

  • Set up or restructure Discord servers, including roles, permissions, bots, onboarding, and guidelines.
  • Write moderation policies, escalation processes, and handbooks, and recruit, train, and support moderators.
  • Handle player reports and community issues, and coach developers on how to engage with their players.

Community health and crisis support

  • Help studios handle toxicity, difficult player conversations, and crisis moments, from drafting a quick Discord post to working with leadership on a decision and next steps.

Creator programs

  • Help studios launch and run creator programs with FirstLook’s creator tools, including onboarding, outreach, and communications.

Build the offering

  • Design service packages for different studio sizes, from self-serve templates to fully embedded support.
  • Track time and outcomes for each engagement so we can price, staff, and scale the offering.
  • Work with sales on scoping and pitching managed services, and with the CSMs who own each studio relationship.
  • Bring product feedback from hands-on use to our Product team, including tools that would help us serve many studios at once.

What we are looking for

  • 4+ years in community management, player operations, or live operations at a game studio or publisher.
  • Hands-on experience running playtests or betas, including recruitment, comms, and feedback collection.
  • Experience building and moderating large Discord communities, including training moderation teams.
  • Comfort with data. You can read funnel and conversion metrics and use them to improve results.
  • The ability to stay calm and clear in hard situations, whether that’s a toxic community or a tough conversation with studio leadership.
  • Strong organization and written communication, with the ability to manage several studios at once.
  • Experience with FirstLook or similar playtesting and community tools.

Helpful experience

  • Consulting or agency work supporting several studios at once.
  • A background in player acquisition, including organic growth and paid channels.
  • Experience running creator or influencer programs.
  • A network across studio community teams.

Why join us
You’ll build a new line of business from the ground up, with real input on how it’s packaged, priced, and delivered. You’ll work directly with studios of all sizes, alongside a small team that knows the product deeply.

We offer remote work and a competitive hourly contract rate, with a path to a full-time role.

jobs.title: Firmware Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About Menlo Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it.
jobs.description:
About Menlo
Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role
You own the software that sits closest to Asimov's hardware, the code that closes control loops on time, every time. You work from bare-metal joint controllers up through embedded Linux on the robot's compute platform, bringing up new boards, writing drivers for the sensors and actuators that make the robot move, and making sure the timing guarantees the controls and autonomy teams depend on actually hold on real hardware.

What You'll Do

  • Design, implement, and test real-time firmware in C/C++ for joint controllers, sensor boards, and power management across the robot

  • Own the embedded Linux platform on Asimov's onboard compute: kernel configuration, device drivers, device trees, and board support packages

  • Bring up new board revisions alongside the electrical team, from first power-on to a fully characterized, controllable subsystem

  • Build and maintain the communication layer between joints and the main compute stack, including bus scheduling, time synchronization, and the joint-level API exposed to controls

  • Own bootloader, flashing, and firmware update flows across every board on the robot, so a fleet-wide update is routine rather than an event

  • Integrate sensors, including IMUs, encoders, force-torque, and camera interfaces, with correct timestamping and deterministic latency

  • Implement safety and fault handling: watchdogs, E-stop paths, thermal and current limits, and graceful degradation when a subsystem drops out

  • Debug across the hardware-software boundary with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and bus sniffers, and build the test automation that catches regressions before they reach a robot

  • Contribute to Menlo's open-source efforts, including firmware, drivers, and hardware bring-up documentation for the broader robotics community

What We Look For

  • 3 or more years of hands-on firmware or embedded software experience on products that ship and run in the real world

  • Strong C and C++ in resource-constrained, real-time environments, plus Python for tooling, test automation, and calibration scripts

  • Practical embedded Linux experience: kernel and driver work, device trees, cross-compilation toolchains, and a build system such as Yocto or Buildroot

  • Solid grounding in real-time systems: interrupt latency, scheduling, jitter, priority inversion, and the discipline to measure timing rather than assume it

  • Deep familiarity with hardware interfaces including SPI, I2C, CAN, UART, and camera interfaces such as MIPI CSI-2 or GMSL

  • Comfort reading schematics and datasheets, and debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD, and bus analyzers

  • Strong communication skills to drive alignment across electrical, mechanical, and controls teams

Nice to Have

  • Experience with bipedal or humanoid robots, legged locomotion platforms, or other high-DOF electromechanical systems

  • Motor control firmware experience: FOC commutation, current/velocity/position loops, encoder calibration, and fault protection

  • RTOS experience (Zephyr, FreeRTOS) or PREEMPT_RT and real-time tuning on Linux

  • Time-sensitive networking, or other deterministic fieldbus and distributed clock synchronization

  • Secure boot, signed images, and over-the-air update infrastructure

  • Familiarity with ROS 2 and how firmware-level data reaches the autonomy stack

  • Hardware-in-the-loop test rigs and CI for firmware

  • Board bring-up experience across multiple hardware revisions of the same product

Why Join Menlo
We are a physical AI company building real robots, and your code is what makes them move. You own the layer closest to the hardware, ship to real robots on a short loop, and open-source what you can for the community building on Asimov. It is a small team with a huge surface area, which means real ownership and the chance to watch your work stand up and walk.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description

We are looking for a skilled Sr. Strategic Delivery Coordinator to lead and drive the delivery of complex Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) and Threat Intelligence engagements. This role will independently manage end-to-end engagement lifecycles, mentor junior team members, and champion process improvement initiatives while providing "Wow Them" service to clients and internal stakeholders.

The Sr. Strategic Delivery Coordinator will be required to demonstrate strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills, serve as a trusted advisor to the Strategic Delivery Manager and Practice Leadership, and leverage deep knowledge of DFIR and GRIT operations to ensure the successful delivery of high-priority engagements across multiple sectors.

About the DFIR & Threat Intelligence Practice:

The DFIR & Threat Intelligence Practice helps organizations prepare for, respond to, and recover from cyber incidents, turning front-line experience into intelligence that keeps clients ahead of the threat. Six specialized teams work as one across the full arc of an incident, from readiness planning through response, recovery, and threat research. We partner with client security and legal teams, cyber insurance carriers, breach counsel, and GuidePoint's regional and sales organizations to cut dwell time and limit business impact.

The six teams:

  • DFIR (Digital Forensics & Incident Response) — Breach investigation, forensics, containment, and eradication when an incident is confirmed or suspected.
  • IRA (Incident Response Advisory) — Readiness before an incident: IR planning, tabletop exercises, Blue Team enablement, and program maturity assessments.
  • GRIT (GuidePoint Research and Intelligence Team) — Original threat research and intelligence that drives our investigations, Threat Actor communications, TI advisory, and as-a-Service capabilities.
  • SD (Strategic Delivery) — Delivery management that keeps engagements staffed, on track, and consistent.
  • R&R (Recovery & Restoration) — Post-incident rebuild that returns clients to safe, operational environments.
  • Insurance & Counsel — The bridge to carriers and breach counsel through the claims and legal side of an incident.

What sets us apart: one integrated practice carries a client through the whole lifecycle with no hand-off gaps, including the demanding parts of an engagement that most providers cannot cover in-house, from GRIT's Threat Actor communications and negotiation support to R&R's full environment restoration and coordination with insurers and counsel. GRIT's research feeds live investigations so our response reflects how adversaries operate now, and established carrier and counsel relationships make GuidePoint a trusted partner across the incident response community.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Independently lead and manage complex, high-visibility DFIR & GRIT engagements end-to-end — from scoping and initiation through closure — with minimal oversight, including resource alignment, deliverable coordination, timeline management, and client communications.
  • Serve as the primary escalation point for critical engagements and client concerns, including active incident response events; coordinate resolution across technical teams, Practice Leadership, and Account Executives where time sensitivity and communication are paramount.
  • Proactively identify and mitigate engagement risks, scope changes, and delivery blockers; escalate to the Strategic Delivery Manager/Practice Lead with recommended courses of action.
  • Coordinate and ensure the quality and consistency of comprehensive engagement deliverables, performing substantive review before client delivery to ensure they are tailored to both technical and managerial audiences.
  • Manage engagement financials awareness including hours tracking, burn rate monitoring, and budget adherence in coordination with the Strategic Delivery Manager.
  • Cultivate and maintain strong, trusted relationships with key client stakeholders by serving as a consistent point of contact and leading client-facing status meetings, kickoff calls, and post-engagement reviews with professional, clear communication at all times.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to expand client engagements or recommend additional GuidePoint services, collaborating with Sales Engineering and Account teams.
  • Lead the design, development, and implementation of repeatable delivery processes, automation, orchestration, and standardization initiatives — including playbooks, templates, checklists, and SOPs — that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability across all DFIR & GRIT engagements.
  • Define and track key delivery metrics and KPIs; generate reporting and analysis to inform Practice Leadership on delivery performance, capacity utilization, and engagement health trends.
  • Mentor and provide day-to-day guidance to Delivery Coordinators, helping them develop their technical knowledge, delivery skills, and professional capabilities.
  • Conduct engagement debriefs, facilitate lessons-learned sessions, and assist with onboarding and training of new team members to promote knowledge sharing and ensure they are equipped with the tools, processes, and context to be effective.
  • Partner with the Strategic Delivery Manager/Practice Lead and other Practice Leadership on capacity planning, resource forecasting, engagement pipeline management, and strategic initiatives including new service offering development, practice growth planning, and organizational process maturity efforts.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales Engineering, Account Executives, Finance/Billing, and Technical Consulting teams to ensure seamless delivery operations.
  • Communicate proactively and regularly with Practice Leadership regarding engagement status, team health, risk posture, and strategic recommendations.
  • Perpetually strengthen relevant skills, knowledge, and abilities to stay at the forefront of the information security industry.
  • Perform other duties, as assigned.

Required Experience and Education:

  • 3-5+ years of experience in project management, delivery coordination, or engagement management within a cybersecurity consulting or managed services environment
  • 2+ years of direct experience working in or supporting Digital Forensics & Incident Response and/or Threat Intelligence operations
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent client engagements end-to-end in a consulting services model
  • Experience with Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR) and Threat Intelligence methodologies, processes, and tooling
  • Proven track record of client relationship management and stakeholder communication at both technical and executive levels
  • Embraces emerging technologies, including AI tools, to work smarter, solve problems, and drive better business outcomes

Preferred Experience and Education

  • Strong understanding of network traffic analysis, host forensics, malware handling/triage, log review, attack surface monitoring, dark web intelligence, threat modeling, and incident response lifecycle methodologies
  • Deep knowledge of industry-related solutions including EDR, NDR, XDR, SIEM, FW, NGAV, Velociraptor, OSQuery, and others
  • Relevant industry certifications strongly preferred, such as PMP, CAPM, SANS GIAC (e.g., GCIH, GCFE, GCFA, GREM, GCTI), CISSP, CISM, or equivalent
  • Experience designing and implementing process improvements, delivery frameworks, or operational workflows
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor, coach, or lead peers in a team environment
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, Visio) and project management/collaboration platforms (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Salesforce/Certinia)
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment

Travel Requirements:

  • Up to 10% travel

Physical Requirements:

  • Sedentary work
  • Substantial movement of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers for a minimum of 8 hours a day
  • Required to have close visual acuity to view computer terminal and/or extensive reading for a minimum of 8 hours a day

GuidePoint Security is a rapidly growing, profitable, privately-held value added reseller that focuses exclusively on Information Security. Since its inception in 2011, GuidePoint has grown to over 1,300 employees, established strategic partnerships with leading security vendors, and serves as a trusted advisor to more than 6,200 customers.

Firmly-defined core values drive all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to the company’s success and establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. This is a unique and rare opportunity to grow your career along with one of the fastest growing companies in the nation.

jobs.description:
Role Summary

Do you want to operate at the edge of innovation—solving mission-critical customer problems, shaping product direction, and deploying AI capabilities where they matter most? If you thrive in fast-moving environments where deep engineering meets real-world customer impact, this role awaits you!

We're looking for an experienced and curious Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join our team. You will serve as the technical vanguard for our largest and most sophisticated customers — deploying Ciroos in enterprise ecosystems, solving real-world production engineering bottlenecks, and translating operational pain into product leverage. This is a customer-facing engineering role where you directly integrate Ciroos into complex, heterogeneous enterprise environments. Your work materially influences our roadmap, accelerates customer adoption, and ensures successful production outcomes. You'll work closely with our product and engineering teams, and our customers, to ensure our AI SRE Teammate delights our customers. You'll be responsible for the availability, operational performance, emergency response, and support for our service that is currently deployed in multiple enterprise production environments. This is an opportunity to be part of a team that is defining a red-hot category (AI in SRE) led by a stellar team with an impeccable track record.

Responsibilities

  • Implement and optimize our AI SRE Teammate to meet the needs of our customers in production and pre-production environments.
  • Proactively monitor customer deployments (with Ciroos!) to ensure that our customers get the best out of the product.
  • Use Ciroos to uncover latent reliability issues (misconfigurations, deployment regressions, scaling) of customer environments.
  • Recommend best practices to customers for implementing the Ciroos AI SRE Teammate in their environment.
  • Plan, design, build, and maintain highly scalable, reliable, and efficient infrastructure for our AI SRE Teammate.
  • Serve as the customer’s technical advocate into engineering and product.
  • Conduct post-incident reviews to identify root causes and implement preventative measures.
  • Ensure security best practices are integrated into customer deployments.
  • Train SRE, Ops, and Platform teams at the customer on how to operate with Ciroos AI SRE Teammate.
  • Lead enterprise migrations onto Ciroos (e.g., replacing incumbent alerting/AIOps platforms such as BigPanda, Moogsoft, PagerDuty, Elastic, or Splunk), including replicating hundreds to thousands of existing correlation rules, running phased cutovers, and hitting hard customer go-live dates.
  • Design, build, and tune alert normalization and correlation policies—writing conditions and operators (IN / CONTAINS / REGEX), extracting fields from noisy sources (email, Jenkins, CI/CD), and choosing tailored playbooks over catch-all rules.
  • Integrate Ciroos with the customer’s operational stack—ticketing (e.g., ServiceNow bi-directional sync and field mapping), collaboration (Microsoft Teams / Slack), observability (Dynatrace, Quantum Metric, Databricks), and knowledge sources (GitHub, Confluence)—including any required app-marketplace certification.
  • Validate and continuously improve investigation quality—diagnosing query-conversion and enrichment errors, unblocking failed investigations, and tuning RCA accuracy so the AI SRE Teammate earns customer trust.
  • Stand up proactive health monitoring for customer deployments (e.g., real-time Slack status channels, SLA-driven alerts on missing metadata or ticket-creation failures) so issues are caught before the customer notices.
  • Own customer-facing communications and delivery artifacts—weekly executive status updates, SLA documents, escalation paths, and migration/scope-change tracking—and coordinate daily syncs with customer project leads.
  • Build long-term technical relationships with senior engineering leaders at customer organizations.
  • Own customer implementations end-to-end—from technical discovery and solution design through production cutover, UAT, go-live, hypercare, and post-launch stabilization—driving execution independently across customer, product, and engineering threads, and demonstrating MTTR reduction and elimination of manual toil.
  • Translate messy, ambiguous customer requirements into clear technical designs, milestones, trade-offs, and acceptance criteria, and keep execution truth legible by making blockers, risks, dependencies, and scope changes explicit early with clear owners and next steps.
  • Design and ship AI-powered investigation and remediation workflows with clear tool boundaries, guardrails, deterministic fallbacks, and human-in-the-loop controls—and define quality controls (versioning, grounding, evals, feedback loops) so the AI SRE Teammate stays trustworthy in production.
  • Ship reusable deployment modules, reference architectures, runbooks, and cutover plans (“golden paths”) that accelerate future customer work and raise delivery repeatability across accounts.
  • Own the value case: set impact hypotheses, baselines, and KPIs (e.g., MTTI/MTTR reduction, toil eliminated), run pre-/post-deployment measurement, and report ROI to executive sponsors.
  • Channel recurring field learnings into roadmap input and product hardening, especially where the same customer pain points show up across deployments.
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous learning and improvement within Ciroos.

Qualifications

  • Customer obsessed: Deep empathy for customers in operational roles such as yours (SREs, ITOps, and DevOps) with a passion to reduce their toil and innovate on their behalf, and always willing to go the extra mile to delight customers.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • At least 6 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, or a similar operational role, including technical leadership or end-to-end ownership of customer-facing delivery. Prior experience in a technical customer success or forward-deployed/solutions engineering role is a strong plus.
  • Strong proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Go, Java).
  • Extensive experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
  • Solid understanding of Kubernetes, infrastructure as code tools (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Intimately familiar with Generative AI, ML concepts and technologies. You must be actively using AI tools to drive your own personal productivity.
  • Strong hands-on experience with observability tools (e.g., Dynatrace, Datadog, Prometheus), ITSM/ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow), and incident management/response systems—including integrating and mapping data between them. Experience migrating a customer off an incumbent AIOps, alerting, or incident-management platform (e.g., BigPanda, Moogsoft, PagerDuty, Elastic, Splunk) is a strong plus.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills to diagnose complex systems systematically, including comfort writing and debugging alert-correlation logic, normalization rules, and regular expressions against messy real-world alert data.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with a collaborative mindset.
  • Track record of independently owning enterprise implementations end-to-end—not just contributing tasks within a larger delivery team—including managing timelines and deliverables, driving daily/weekly customer syncs, and producing executive-facing status updates and SLA documentation, with strong customer outcomes and minimal execution drift.
  • Strong integration and data experience: APIs, webhooks, event-driven systems, schema alignment, transformations, retries/idempotency, reliable error handling, and end-to-end integration configuration (field mapping, bi-directional sync, SSO/SAML)—including, where required, taking apps through marketplace certification (e.g., ServiceNow Store, Microsoft Teams).
  • Hands-on experience designing and delivering production-grade AI/automation workflows, ideally LLM-powered, with practical guardrails and evaluation approaches.
  • Comfort with enterprise security and architecture requirements—RBAC, encryption, auditability, private networking, identity, and data-handling expectations.
  • Calm, high-judgment execution in ambiguous, fast-moving customer environments, moving fluidly between system-level architecture and execution-level detail.
  • Intrinsically curious and able to thrive amid ambiguity, shifting customer scope, and hard deadlines—driving projects to completion while keeping enterprise stakeholders aligned.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with operating/supporting customers running AI infrastructure or AI tools.
  • Familiarity with incumbent alerting/AIOps and incident-management platforms (e.g., BigPanda, Moogsoft, PagerDuty, Elastic, Splunk), and the realities of migrating correlation rules and operational workflows off them.
  • Experience building lightweight internal tooling and automation (Python/Node/bash) to accelerate validation, migration, and monitoring.

What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months)

In your first 6–12 months, success in this role looks like:

  • You’ve owned one or more enterprise deployments end-to-end—discovery through go-live and hypercare—with strong customer outcomes and minimal execution drift.
  • Your customers trust you, know what to expect, and are operating the Ciroos AI SRE Teammate confidently on their own.
  • Risks, blockers, dependencies, and scope changes stay explicit and current across your accounts—no surprises reach the customer without a plan.
  • You’ve demonstrably reduced customer toil and incident time (e.g., measurable MTTI/MTTR improvement) and reported it against a clear baseline.
  • You’ve improved delivery repeatability by shipping at least one reusable pattern, reference architecture, or runbook the wider team now uses.
  • You’ve turned recurring field pain into concrete product feedback that shaped the roadmap or hardened the platform.

About Ciroos

Ciroos (pronounced “Sai rose”) is a seed-stage startup founded in February 2025 by a team of experienced executives and distinguished engineers with deep expertise in observability, AI, distributed systems, cloud, cybersecurity, and networking. Our mission is to provide an AI SRE Teammate that empowers SREs to be superheroes. Our AI SRE Teammate is based on a multi-agentic AI platform that uses expert human-like reasoning to decrease toil, investigate incidents faster, and drive autonomous operations for SREs. To date, we have raised $21M in seed funding led by Energy Impact Partners and several prominent angel investors. We are headquartered in Pleasanton, CA with operations in India.

Why Work at Ciroos?

At Ciroos, our mission is to provide an AI SRE Teammate that empowers SREs to be superheroes. We dream big and execute fast. Build. Test. Iterate. All at lightning speed in service of our customers. Tickle your curiosity and shape the future of agentic AI for SREs!

We work hard and play hard. Our “BEST” perks are designed to help you operate at your peak potential in a fun environment:

  • Benefits: Comprehensive medical, vision, and dental benefits. 401k plans and commuter benefits. Free lunches, snacks, and top-of-the-line espressos!
  • Equity: Equity that could change your life, not just look nice on paper. QSBS eligibility for US employees
  • Stewardship: A career-defining, high-impact role with plenty of mentorship opportunities from founders and other coworkers
  • Teamwork: Collaborative coworkers with high IQ and high EQ. No politics. No bureaucracy. No permission-seeking

Ciroos is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
About Us

Red Cell Partners is an incubation firm building and investing in rapidly scalable technology-led companies that are bringing revolutionary advancements to market in three distinct practice areas: healthcare, cyber, and national security. United by a shared sense of duty and deep belief in the power of innovation, Red Cell is developing powerful tools and solutions to address our Nation’s most pressing problems.

About the Role

We're hiring a mid-level Product Designer to own end-to-end design on one or more product areas. You will work directly with engineers, product, and subject-matter experts to turn ambiguous operational problems into interfaces that are dense, fast, and legible. This is a hands-on role: you will be in Figma, in the design system, and in code review conversations, not just in strategy decks.

You will work in a small team with a short distance between design and shipped software and direct contact with the people who use what we build. Designers have meaningful ownership of their product areas and are expected to bring informed opinions to the work.

This is a 1099 contract opportunity, with expected 40 hours per week. A Secret Clearance is required.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the design of features from discovery through shipped implementation — problem framing, flows, wireframes, high-fidelity UI, and design QA.
  • Design for complexity: data-dense tables, map and timeline views, simulation outputs, and multi-role workflows where information hierarchy is the whole job.
  • Contribute to and extend our design system (@defcon/ui) — build components in Figma, define tokens and variants, and partner with engineering on the React/TypeScript implementation.
  • Run lightweight discovery with SMEs and end users, working within the access constraints of government environments. Translate what you learn into shared artifacts the team actually uses.
  • Design the unglamorous but critical parts of government software: authentication flows (CAC/PIV), role-based access control, permissions, empty and error states, and audit-friendly interactions.
  • Meet accessibility requirements as a baseline, not a cleanup pass — WCAG 2.1 AA and Section 508 compliance.
  • Give and receive critique. Present work clearly to non-designers, including customers and program stakeholders.

Required Qualifications

  • 4–5 years of product design experience shipping software, supported by a portfolio that demonstrates your process and decision-making, not just final screens.
  • Strong proficiency in Figma, including components, variants, auto-layout, and variables.
  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining a design system, including defining tokens and component APIs, documenting usage, communicating version changes, managing deprecations, and keeping the design library aligned with its coded implementation.
  • Experience designing complex, information-dense applications, such as enterprise, analytics, logistics, or operational tools. Portfolios focused exclusively on consumer products may be less aligned with this role.
  • Working knowledge of front-end concepts, including component structure, state, responsive behavior, and design tokens, with the ability to collaborate effectively with engineers and identify implementation drift.
  • Experience using discovery, user research, or competitive analysis to inform design decisions and solve product problems.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to translate business goals into functional design solutions, explain trade-offs, and respectfully challenge decisions when needed.
  • Ability to work independently through standard design challenges while recognizing when to seek guidance on complex architectural or system-scaling decisions.
  • Strong storytelling, presentation, written, and asynchronous communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate design rationale and build alignment across teams, time zones, and security boundaries.
  • Active Secret clearance and U.S. citizenship required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • A clearance above Secret (Top Secret or TS/SCI).
  • Prior work on defense, government, or other regulated or compliance-heavy products.
  • Experience contributing code to a design system or front-end codebase (React, TypeScript, CSS).
  • Familiarity with map-based interfaces, scheduling and timeline UI, or simulation and modeling tools.
  • Experience designing for classified or air-gapped environments, or working within FedRAMP and IL5 constraints.

Compensation: This is a 1099 independent contractor position. Compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, scope of work, and anticipated level of effort.

  • Career track opportunity with potential for rapid advancement with strong performance as the firm grows
  • 100% employer paid, comprehensive health care including medical, dental, and vision for you and your family.

jobs.description:
Mission

EdReports.org is at the forefront of the curriculum reform movement. By increasing the capacity of educators to identify and demand the highest quality curriculum, EdReports.org is both disrupting a multibillion-dollar market and transforming the way students are taught and ultimately perform. With the firm belief that what is taught matters and that all students deserve high quality materials, EdReports.org publishes free, online, evidence-rich reviews of instructional materials. Explore our organization's core competencies in greater detail here.

Planning to use Artificial Intelligence (AI) for your application, interview prep, or for other means of assistance throughout the hiring process? Click here to review our AI guidance before proceeding.

Purpose of Position

The Vice President, Enterprise Transformation & Delivery leads EdReports' enterprise portfolio execution, organizational performance, culture strategy, and transformation. This leader owns the systems, practices, and capabilities that translate approved strategic priorities into coordinated delivery, measurable results, and sustained organizational improvement.

Reporting to the CEO and serving on the Executive Team, the Vice President oversees enterprise portfolio delivery, execution governance, organizational performance reporting, and accountability mechanisms. This leader also shapes organizational culture, leads internal communications and change management, and builds organizational learning and leadership capabilities that strengthen effectiveness across EdReports.

As an executive partner, the Vice President advises the CEO and Executive Team on execution risks, organizational capacity, performance, and change readiness while building the systems and alignment needed to achieve EdReports' mission.

Key Responsibilities & Outcomes

Responsibilities:

  • Enterprise Execution Strategy and Governance: Establish and lead EdReports' enterprise execution strategy, translating approved organizational priorities into coordinated commitments, performance expectations, and accountability mechanisms. Own the operation and continuous improvement of execution governance within the enterprise governance architecture developed collaboratively by the CEO and Executive Team.
  • Health Dashboard and Organizational Performance Reporting: Own the development, management, and organizational adoption of EdReports' Health Dashboard as the central mechanism for enterprise execution visibility. Integrate strategic, financial, talent, operational, and portfolio measures in partnership with functional data owners, establish reporting standards, and provide actionable insights for executive decisions. Lead the transition of existing dashboard and reporting responsibilities into the function.
  • Enterprise Performance and Execution Accountability: Establish operational performance standards and lead enterprise execution reviews to evaluate delivery, organizational capacity, risks, and progress against commitments. Strengthen accountability for agreed actions and corrective measures through established governance processes, while preserving functional leaders' authority over their teams and results.
  • Executive Advisory and Decision Support: Serve as a senior execution advisor to the CEO and Executive Team, shaping recommendations on delivery feasibility, organizational capacity, implementation investments, and execution trade-offs. Challenge assumptions, evaluate options, and surface institutional risks that affect organizational performance and change readiness.
  • Enterprise Portfolio Governance and Delivery: Direct enterprise portfolio intake, sequencing, delivery oversight, dependency management, and escalation within approved strategic priorities and resource parameters. Exercise delegated authority to resolve cross-functional execution barriers and recommend adjustments when competing commitments exceed organizational capacity.
  • Organizational Effectiveness and Operating Model Implementation: Lead implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement of practices within the enterprise operating model designed in partnership with the CEO and Executive Team. Build cross-functional workflows, operating standards, tools, and accountability practices; assess their effectiveness; and recommend systemic improvements through established decision channels.
  • Organizational Culture and Institutional Health: Own EdReports' enterprise culture strategy, translating core values and DBIE commitments into organizational priorities, leadership expectations, and measurable initiatives. Partner with People, which owns Lattice and employee engagement measurement systems, to evaluate culture outcomes, address systemic challenges, and strengthen organizational trust and resilience.
  • Organizational Learning and Leadership Capability: Shape and lead enterprise learning, leadership development, and capability-building initiatives that address organizational needs, strengthen management effectiveness, and support execution readiness. Partner with People to connect organizational learning priorities with talent management, employee performance insights, and workforce needs.
  • Enterprise Transformation and Change Management: Lead implementation and institutionalization of major strategic and organizational changes sponsored through approved executive governance. Establish change readiness, stakeholder engagement, communication, and adoption practices; coordinate cross-functional implementation; and advise the CEO on organizational risks and barriers to sustained change.
  • Internal Communications and Enterprise Alignment: Own EdReports' internal communications strategy and operating rhythm, organizational updates, and change communications. Partner with the CEO, Chief of Staff, People, and Communications as appropriate to ensure consistent messaging, transparency, and understanding of organizational priorities and decisions.
  • Executive Partnership and Functional Leadership: Build and lead the Enterprise Execution & Organizational Effectiveness function, establishing its long-term direction, capabilities, standards, and performance expectations. Lead through managers and senior professionals, steward functional resources, and partner with executive peers to strengthen enterprise execution while preserving their respective decision-making authority.
  • Other relevant duties as assigned to support the organization's strategic goals, with the expectation that all EdReports employees remain flexible and adaptable to evolving responsibilities.

Outcomes:

  • Reliable Enterprise Delivery: Strategic priorities translate into coordinated plans, clear accountability, and consistent execution.
  • Effective Portfolio Governance: Initiatives are sequenced and delivered through consistent practices that surface dependencies, risks, and capacity constraints.
  • Actionable Performance Visibility: The Health Dashboard and execution reviews provide timely, reliable insights into organizational performance and delivery health.
  • Stronger Execution Accountability: Leaders address barriers, follow through on commitments, and take corrective action.
  • Improved Organizational Effectiveness: Enterprise operating practices strengthen coordination, efficiency, accountability, and execution quality.
  • Intentional Organizational Culture: Culture initiatives reinforce EdReports' values and DBIE commitments, with progress evaluated through employee feedback and engagement data.
  • Stronger Organizational Capabilities: Learning and leadership development initiatives improve management effectiveness, collaboration, and organizational readiness.
  • Sustained Transformation: Major changes are implemented effectively and adopted into ongoing organizational practices.
  • Clear Internal Communications: Employees receive consistent, timely communications that strengthen understanding, transparency, and alignment.
  • Sustainable Execution Capability: EdReports has the systems, leadership, and capabilities needed to execute priorities and adapt to change.

Travel

National travel will occur related to organizational needs and for professional learning, as needed. Amount of travel will be monitored to ensure it is appropriate for both the organization and this role.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Passion for EdReports’ mission, vision, core values, and our commitment to Diversity, Belonging, Inclusion, and Equity;
  • Typically ten or more years of relevant strategic professional experience, including eight or more years of progressive people management experience, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
  • Extensive executive or senior leadership experience spanning enterprise execution, organizational effectiveness, portfolio governance, organizational development, or large-scale change management.
  • Demonstrated success designing, establishing, and leading enterprise-wide operating systems, governance frameworks, or organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Proven ability to navigate complex organizational challenges, resolve competing priorities, and influence senior executive decision-makers.
  • Strong business acumen and demonstrated ability to integrate strategic, financial, workforce, and organizational considerations into enterprise recommendations.
  • Experience establishing functional policies, leading multiple teams or functional areas, and developing managers and senior leaders.
  • Deep knowledge of organizational culture, enterprise change adoption, operating effectiveness, and organizational performance improvement.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trust, lead through ambiguity, exercise sound executive judgment, and drive accountability across organizational boundaries.
  • Exceptional communication, executive advisory, facilitation, and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Residency in and authorization to work in the United States.

Preferred:

  • Experience in a mission-driven nonprofit, education organization, or similarly complex environment.
  • Experience building and institutionalizing enterprise-wide execution and organizational effectiveness capabilities.
  • Experience advising CEOs or executive leadership teams on organizational transformation, enterprise governance, or systemic operating improvements.

Salary

The salary for this position is $148,064 - $222,095 annually. At EdReports, we determine final salaries based on the role's requirements and the candidate's experience and skills, while maintaining equity within our compensation bands. To support fairness and provide opportunities for growth, we typically offer salaries at or below the midpoint of the range. All salary offers are non-negotiable to ensure consistency and equity across the organization.

Benefits

We know the importance of living a fulfilling, healthy life–both professionally and personally. That’s why some of the benefits we offer include:

  • Unlimited Discretionary Time Off (DTO) and Sick Time,
  • 21 days of paid holidays and office closure days in 2026,
  • Monthly Communications Reimbursement,
  • Initial home office and technology setup stipend,
  • EdReports pays for 90% of health care for both the employee and their immediate family, and
  • 401k that new hires become eligible for after six months of employment (includes safe harbor, employer match, etc.).

Work Authorization Requirements

All EdReports employees must reside in and be authorized to work in the United States. EdReports does not sponsor employment visas, and we are unable to consider candidates residing outside the U.S.

Physical Requirements

Work is normally performed in a remote office environment including, but not limited to standing and sitting for long periods of time; and fine-finger and hand manipulation to operate a computer and keyboard. Employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as preparing and analyzing electronic information, transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, and extensive reading. This person will travel by car, air, or other transportation (as indicated in the Travel section) and should be able to physically withstand the demands of such travel. Employee may be required to walk for long distances at retreat venues or other relevant sites.

Core Competencies

  • COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, BELONGING, INCLUSION, AND EQUITY: Actively welcome diverse perspectives, center equity in decision-making, foster authentic and inclusive relationships that promote a sense of belonging, confront biases to build understanding, and continuously build knowledge of systemic inequities to inform behaviors that lead to an inclusive organizational culture.
  • ACCOUNTABILITY: Proficiently organize projects aligned with overarching objectives while proactively addressing challenges; ensure timely and high-quality fulfillment of responsibilities.
  • COMMUNICATION: Effectively engage stakeholders, actively listen to others, convey information for desired results, and adapt style to foster relationships and trust.
  • CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT: Consistently reflect, seek feedback, and apply new insights; identify and implement solutions that enhance individual, team, and overall performance.
  • CORE EXPERTISE: Possess skills, knowledge, and abilities to perform essential duties; keeps knowledge current; utilize multiple points of view to achieve goals and is a subject matter resource for others.
  • ORGANIZATIONAL STEWARDSHIP: Cultivate external relationships, uphold policies, leverage historical insights, actively participate in organizational improvement, and adapt to align with the needs of the organization.

Manager & Senior Leader Competencies

  • EMPATHETIC LEADERSHIP: Cultivate and lead an environment of reflection, feedback, clear expectations, and support that drives individual and team excellence; manage with compassion and kindness by adapting leadership style to meet an individual’s needs.
  • STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT: Adeptly address complex issues, engage others in decision-making and change initiatives; skillfully communicate information to foster team success; inspire momentum through purposeful direction.
  • RESOURCE MANAGEMENT: Thoughtfully allocate, monitor, and reflect to optimize resource utilization and enhance overall effectiveness.

We Value All Voices

EdReports is committed to equal-employment principles and we recognize the value of committed employees who feel they are being treated in an equitable and professional manner. We strive to find ways to attract, develop, and retain the talent needed to meet business objectives, and to recruit and employ highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities in which we live, work, and serve. As such, all employment decisions at EdReports are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status, family or parental status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

We are also committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the selection process, please direct your inquiries to our HR department at .
